version: SEBI/HO/ITD-1/ITD_CSC_EXT/P/CIR/2024/113 v1.0, read with CIR/2024/184, CIR/2025/60, CIR/2025/96, CIR/2025/119 and FAQs of 11 Jun 2025

groups.title: Thresholds for REs' categorization (read with CIR/2025/60 and CIR/2025/119 Part-C)

controls.title: Determine the CSCRF category of the RE annually from prior-year data
controls.prose: CSCRF follows a graded approach and classifies REs into five categories: Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs: stock exchanges, depositories, clearing corporations and QRTAs; KRAs were moved from the MII bucket to Qualified REs by CIR/2025/60 clause 2.5), Qualified REs, Mid-size REs, Small-size REs and Self-certification REs. The category shall be decided at the beginning of the financial year based on the data of the previous financial year, shall not change during the year irrespective of changes in the parameters, and shall be validated by the reporting authority at the time of compliance submission. Where an RE is registered under more than one category, the provisions of the highest category apply (Section 2 para 23; FAQ Q24). Thresholds by entity type are stated in Section 2 Tables 3-13 as revised by CIR/2025/60 (stock brokers: Qualified above 10 lakh registered clients or above Rs 10,00,000 crore annual clientele trading volume, Mid-size above 1 lakh clients or Rs 1,00,000 crore, Small-size above 10,000 clients or Rs 10,000 crore, Self-certification above 1,000 clients or Rs 1,000 crore, exempt below 1,000 clients and Rs 1,000 crore; DPs that are banks, NBFCs, MFs, RTAs, custodians, clearing corporations or financial institutions are Qualified REs; MFs/AMCs Qualified at Rs 1 lakh crore AUM, Mid-size at Rs 10,000 crore, Small-size below; custodians Qualified at Rs 10 lakh crore AUC, Mid-size at Rs 1 lakh crore; AIF/VCF managers Mid-size at Rs 10,000 crore aggregate corpus, Small-size above Rs 3,000 crore, Self-certification at or below Rs 3,000 crore; portfolio managers per CIR/2025/119 Part-C Mid-size at Rs 10,000 crore AUM, Small-size above Rs 3,000 crore, Self-certification at or below Rs 3,000 crore; active merchant bankers Small-size and inactive ones exempt; RTAs Mid-size at 1 crore folios, Small-size at 10,000 folios; non-individual IAs Small-size, and IAs/RAs registered in no other capacity exempt; CIS, CRAs and active DTs Self-certification; BTI/SCSBs submit a certificate of compliance with RBI cybersecurity guidelines; FPIs, FVCIs, LPCC, QDPs, REITs/InvITs and vault managers excluded).
controls.guidance: Record the category as company details.regulatoryRegistrations[].category using the shared reCategory slugs (mii, qualified-re, mid-size-re, small-size-re, self-certification-re) with the financial year and the parameter values that justify it; refresh-ctx re-derives the category each April from the prior-year client count, trading volume, AUM/AUC, corpus or folio figures and raises an observation when the recorded category is lower than the derived one. Every other control in this catalog intersects its applicability.reCategories with this value, so an incorrect category silently changes the whole control set. For multi-registration entities keep one category equal to the highest applicable.
evidenceExpected: Board or IT Committee minute recording the CSCRF category for the financial year with the prior-year parameter values
Reporting-authority validation of the category at compliance submission
SEBI registration list showing every capacity in which the RE is registered

params.label: CSCRF category of the RE for the current financial year
Financial year whose data determined the category

controls.title: Apply the M-SOC and SOC-service exemptions for very small client bases
controls.prose: CSCRF mandates SOC services for all REs except client-based stock brokers having fewer than 100 clients (Box Item 11; DE.CM guideline 1(c)). CIR/2025/60 further exempts DPs with fewer than 100 clients (clause 2.2) and RTAs with fewer than 100 clients (clause 3) from the requirement of employing SOC services or on-boarding to Market-SOC. For self-certification portfolio managers with fewer than 100 clients (clause 2.6) and self-certification AIF/VCF managers with a client base below 100 (clause 2.7) the circular exempts only the mandatory Market-SOC (M-SOC) requirement; their general obligation to employ SOC services (own, group or third-party SOC) remains. Small-size and self-certification REs that operate their own or a group SOC may rely on it instead of M-SOC but must still submit the SOC efficacy report periodically (FAQ Q59-Q60; CIR/2025/119 clause 6.9).
controls.guidance: Store the client count that supports any SOC exemption alongside the category in details.json. Cite this control in an observation that waives DE.CM.S1-S3 evidence only for client-based stock brokers, DPs and RTAs with fewer than 100 clients. For self-certification portfolio managers and AIF/VCF managers below 100 clients waive only the M-SOC onboarding evidence and still require evidence of own, group or third-party SOC coverage under DE.CM.S1-S3. The exemption lapses the year the client count crosses 100, so refresh-ctx re-checks it annually. The Table 25/26 standard exemptions for small, self-certification and mid-size REs are conditional on M-SOC onboarding, so a small RE that is neither on M-SOC nor exempt loses those exemptions.
evidenceExpected: Client count as at 31 March of the previous financial year
M-SOC onboarding confirmation from NSE or BSE, or the group SOC efficacy report

params.label: Client count below which the SOC-service or M-SOC exemption applies (scope depends on entity type)

controls.title: Constitute an IT Committee for REs with an external independent cybersecurity expert
controls.prose: MIIs (through SCOT), MFs/AMCs (through the Technology Committee), Qualified REs and Mid-size REs shall constitute an IT Committee for REs which mandatorily includes at least one external independent expert on cybersecurity (Section 3.2-3.3). Its terms of reference include periodic review of implementation of the cybersecurity and cyber resilience policy, review of incidents, their impact, RCA and plans to prevent recurrence, deliberation on matters referred by the Board or SEBI, and review of CSCRF compliances with recommendations to the Board (Section 3.5). The committee shall meet quarterly (Table 15 item 5; GV.PO guideline 9). Small-size and self-certification REs need not constitute one; their CSCRF compliance is reviewed and approved by the MD/CEO, a Board member, partners or proprietor (Section 3.4). CIR/2025/119 Table 2 lists this constitution among controls where an equivalent primary-regulator committee satisfies the principle of equivalence.
controls.guidance: Evidence the committee charter, the independent expert's appointment letter and quarterly minutes in the company summary governance section; refresh-soc records a control record with parameter itCommitteeMeetingsPerYear and raises a finding when fewer than four meetings are minuted in a financial year or the external expert is absent. Every VAPT report, cyber audit report, red-team result, resilience-test result and incident RCA in this catalog must show the date it was placed before this committee.
evidenceExpected: IT Committee charter or Board resolution naming members including the external independent cybersecurity expert
Quarterly minutes covering policy implementation review, incident review and CSCRF compliance recommendations
For MIIs and AMCs, SCOT or Technology Committee terms of reference addendum

params.label: Minimum IT Committee meetings per financial year (quarterly)

groups.title: CSCRF Compliance, Audit Report Submission, and Timelines

controls.title: Report CSCRF compliance to the reporting authority at the stated periodicities
controls.prose: Unless specified otherwise, compliance reporting for CSCRF is made to the RE's existing reporting authority: MIIs and most REs to SEBI, stock brokers to stock exchanges, depository participants to depositories, and IAs/RAs to BSE Ltd (as IAASB/RAASB) for five years from 25 July 2024 per CIR/2025/60 clause 2.4.1. Table 15 fixes the periodicities of the recurring standards: CCI third-party assessment half-yearly for MIIs and self-assessment annually for Qualified REs with evidence submitted within 15 days of completion; policy review annually; IT Committee meetings quarterly; threat-based risk assessment half-yearly for MIIs and annually for Qualified and Mid-size REs; access-rights and privileged-activity reviews quarterly for MIIs and Qualified REs and half-yearly for others; training annually; review of third-party managed systems half-yearly for MIIs and Qualified REs and annually for others; SOC efficacy half-yearly for MIIs and Qualified REs and annually for M-SOC or third-party SOC users; red teaming half-yearly; threat hunting quarterly; recovery-plan drills half-yearly for MIIs and Qualified REs and annually for others; contingency plan review half-yearly for MIIs and Qualified REs and annually for Mid-size and Small-size REs; cyber resilience posture evaluation annually for Mid-size and Small-size REs. All periodicities are based on the financial year (FAQ Q20, Q34) and compliance with all standards is submitted along with the cyber audit report. Auditors validate adherence to these periodicities during cyber audit.
controls.guidance: refresh-soc computes, for every control in this catalog with a cadence, the next due date from the last observation and the financial-year anchor (1 April) and marks the control overdue when the cadence window closes without an observation; report-audit-findings renders the Table 15 periodicity table with actual versus required frequency in the regulatory posture section. Keep the reporting authority per registration in details.json so the report names the correct recipient.
evidenceExpected: Compliance submission acknowledgements from SEBI, the exchange, the depository or BSE Ltd
Calendar of Table 15 activities for the financial year with completion dates

params.label: Days after CCI assessment completion to submit evidence

controls.title: ISO 27001 certification for MIIs, with evidence submitted alongside the cyber audit
controls.prose: MIIs shall obtain ISO 27001 (latest version) certification within one year of issuance of CSCRF (standard PR.IP.S16) and submit the certification evidence to SEBI along with the cyber audit report (Table 16; for context only, Table 16 routes stock broker and depository participant submissions to the stock exchanges or depositories, which does not arise under this MII-only control). CSCRF originally extended the mandate to Qualified REs; CIR/2025/119 clause 6.11 clarified that Qualified REs are encouraged and recommended, but not mandated, to obtain ISO 27001. The certification scope shall include at least the primary data centre, DR site, near-DR site, SOC and colocation facility, and any of these outsourced to a third party must also be ISO 27001 certified for the outsourced service (PR.IP.S16 guideline; FAQ Q58).
controls.guidance: Record the certificate number, issuing body, scope statement and expiry as parameters on the control record and attach the certificate as workspace evidence; refresh-soc raises a finding when the certificate has lapsed, when the scope statement omits PDC, DR, NDR, SOC or colocation, or when an outsourced site's provider (vendors/<vendor_id>.json) lacks a certificate covering the outsourced service. For Qualified REs Maxwell records the certificate as an info observation only, since CIR/2025/119 made it recommendatory. Sec-4.2 is the single finding carrier for the ISO 27001 obligation; PR.IP.S16 is evidence-only, so never raise a second finding under PR.IP.S16 for the same certificate.
evidenceExpected: ISO/IEC 27001 certificate with scope covering PDC, DR, NDR, SOC and colocation
Surveillance or recertification audit report within the certificate cycle
Submission acknowledgement of the certificate with the cyber audit report
ISO 27001 certificates of third parties operating any in-scope site

params.label: Months from CSCRF issuance for MIIs to obtain ISO 27001

controls.title: VAPT periodicity, report submission within one month and closure within three months
controls.prose: REs shall plan VAPT at the beginning of the financial year so that no audit cycle is left unaudited on a change of category. REs identified as Protected Systems or CII by NCIIPC shall complete at least two VAPT activities per year, one in each half of the financial year including report submission, closure and revalidation; all other REs at least once, commencing in the first quarter (Table 18). Qualified Stock Brokers conduct VAPT half-yearly irrespective of category (FAQ Q14). The VAPT report shall be submitted after approval by the IT Committee for REs within one month of completion; findings shall be closed within three months of report submission following a graded approach by criticality; revalidation shall be completed within five months of completion (Table 19). Open vulnerabilities after three months shall be approved by the IT Committee and closed before the next VAPT; a risk register shall be maintained (4.3.4-4.3.5). Reports follow the Annexure-A format with an MD/CEO declaration, are submitted to exchanges/depositories by stock brokers and DPs, to BASL/BSE by IAs, and to SEBI by MIIs and the rest (Table 17). Only the summary is submitted; explicit vulnerabilities are never submitted unless SEBI asks (CIR/2025/119 clause 6.7). Closure of third-party application vulnerabilities is also due within three months (FAQ Q15).
controls.guidance: Every soc finding whose source is the annual or half-yearly VAPT carries slaBasis topic vapt-cadence and a dueAt of report submission plus 90 days; refresh-soc reconciles auditor findings by fingerprint and flags any finding still open at 90 days that lacks an IT Committee approval reference. Store the VAPT report submission date, the revalidation date and the IT Committee approval date as parameters on the control record. Maxwell never stores the explicit vulnerability list in summary.md; keep it in the ledger only.
evidenceExpected: Annexure-A VAPT report with auditor declaration, scope table and MD/CEO declaration
IT Committee minutes approving the report and any exclusions
Closure and revalidation report showing every finding closed within three months or approved as open
Risk register entries for open observations

params.label: Months after VAPT completion to submit the report
Months after report submission to close VAPT findings
Months after VAPT completion to complete revalidation
Minimum VAPT activities per financial year (2 for CII/Protected Systems and QSBs, 1 otherwise)

controls.title: Cyber audit periodicity, coverage, submission within one month and closure within three months
controls.prose: Cyber audit verifies compliance with CSCRF and shall cover 100 percent of critical systems and 25 percent of non-critical systems on a sample basis. MIIs, Qualified REs, and Mid-size and Small-size REs that provide IBT or algorithmic trading facilities shall conduct cyber audit at least twice a year; the rest of the REs at least once a year (Table 21); QSBs half-yearly (FAQ Q14). The final report shall be submitted after IT Committee approval within one month of completion, open observations closed within three months of submission with a graded approach, and a follow-on audit completed within five months (Table 22). Open observations after three months shall be approved by the IT Committee and closed before the next audit; the follow-on audit report and open observations are placed before the IT Committee (4.4.4-4.4.5). Reports follow Annexure-B with the MD/CEO declaration and control-wise compliance status for every standard from GV.OC.S1 to EV.ST.S5 plus the exception-reporting format. Self-certification REs conduct only VAPT and submit the Annexure-P self-certification signed by the authorised signatory (4.4.6). Audits from FY 2025-26 onward are conducted against CSCRF read with its clarifications (CIR/2025/60 clause 10). Exchanges and depositories must keep member reports confidential (CIR/2025/119 clause 6.12).
controls.guidance: refresh-soc ingests the Annexure-B control-wise table as one observation per CSCRF standard id and one finding per non-conformity with dueAt of submission plus 90 days; report-audit-findings reproduces the exception-reporting columns (IT Committee comment, Board comment, repeat in last three audits) from ledger fields. Compare the audit sample against the metastore critical-system list to confirm 100 percent critical coverage and record the non-critical sampling rationale.
evidenceExpected: Annexure-B cyber audit report with auditor declaration, scope, control-wise status and exception table
IT Committee minutes approving the report
Follow-on audit report within five months and closure evidence for each observation
Coverage reconciliation showing all critical systems audited

params.label: Minimum cyber audits per financial year (2 for MIIs, Qualified REs, QSBs and IBT/algo providers; 1 otherwise)
Months after report submission to close audit observations
Share of critical systems covered by cyber audit
Share of non-critical systems sampled in cyber audit

controls.title: Market SOC set up by NSE and BSE and audited annually
controls.prose: The Market SOC shall be set up mandatorily by NSE and BSE and optionally by NSDL and/or CDSL by 1 January 2025, in accordance with CSCRF, and shall ensure that participating REs comply with CSCRF as applicable to them. NSE and BSE (and NSDL/CDSL if applicable) shall audit their Market SOC activity annually and submit the report to SEBI, and the functional efficacy of the Market SOC measured per Annexure-N shall be reported along with the provider's cyber audit report. Market SOC shall also provide VAPT and cyber audit services to small-size and mid-size REs at affordable cost through CERT-In empanelled auditors, evolve with new SEBI guidelines and ensure participants adhere to minimum IT guidelines, while accountability for compliance rests with the participating REs (Section 4.5; Box Item 11).
controls.guidance: Applies only to MIIs operating an M-SOC. For NSE/BSE profiles, refresh-soc records the annual M-SOC audit and Annexure-N efficacy score; for participating REs the M-SOC onboarding certificate and annual efficacy report are evidence under DE.CM.S1 and DE.CM.S3.
evidenceExpected: Annual Market SOC audit report submitted to SEBI
Annexure-N functional efficacy report of the Market SOC
Onboarding register of participating REs

controls.title: Understand and communicate the critical services external stakeholders depend on
controls.prose: Critical objectives, capabilities and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the RE shall be understood and communicated. The guideline for GV.OC.S2-S3 adds that cybersecurity roles and responsibilities are coordinated with internal roles and external partners, and that the RE defines the responsibilities of its own employees, third-party service providers' employees and other entities with privileged access to its systems.
controls.guidance: Capture the critical services and the stakeholders that depend on them in details.json (business lines, MII connectivity, client-facing channels) and link each to the critical systems in sdlc/metastore.json so that criticality classification under ID.AM.S4 traces back to a business service. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Business service catalogue naming external stakeholders and dependent services
Responsibility matrix covering employees, third-party staff and privileged external entities

controls.title: Understand and manage legal and regulatory cybersecurity, data protection and privacy requirements
controls.prose: Legal and regulatory requirements regarding cybersecurity, including data protection and data privacy, shall be understood and managed. The mandatory guideline requires all REs to comply with cybersecurity and data-protection requirements in laws, circulars and regulations issued by SEBI and GoI such as the IT Act 2000 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, to conduct audits and inspections of their own and their sub-contractors' IT resources (or engage a third-party auditor), to permit SEBI or any government agency to search and seize IT resources and data including those held by third-party service providers, to engage a forensic auditor to identify the root cause of any incident, and to furnish audit reports to SEBI on request.
controls.guidance: refresh-ctx maintains the applicable-instrument set for the company (this catalog, cert-in-directions-2022, dpdp-rules-2025, RBI or IRDAI instruments for multi-regulated groups) and records drift when a new SEBI circular is published; every third-party contract reviewed by refresh-vendor-ctx must carry the SEBI access, search-and-seizure and audit-report clauses. Findings against any other instrument cite this control when the gap is one of not having identified the obligation.
evidenceExpected: Register of applicable laws, circulars and regulations with owner and last review date
Contract clauses granting SEBI access to data and IT resources held by third parties
Internal or third-party audit and inspection reports of IT resources

controls.title: Understand and communicate dependency on third-party service providers
controls.prose: REs shall understand and communicate the outcomes, capabilities and services that depend on external resources such as third-party service providers.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx populates company-profile/<c>/vendors/<vendor_id>.json with the services each provider delivers and the critical systems they touch; an observation records any critical system in the metastore with no vendor dependency mapped or a vendor with no owner. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Vendor register linking each provider to the services and critical systems it supports
Communication of dependencies to the IT Committee or Board

controls.title: Leadership accountability for cybersecurity risk and a risk-aware culture
controls.prose: The responsibility and accountability for cybersecurity risk lies with the RE's leadership, which is responsible for nurturing a culture that is risk-aware, cybersecurity conscious and continually improving.
controls.guidance: Evidence through Board or partner-level minutes that receive the cybersecurity policy, incident reviews and audit outcomes; the MD/CEO declarations on the Annexure-A and Annexure-B reports are the primary artefacts. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Board or partner minutes showing cybersecurity items on the agenda
MD/CEO declarations accompanying VAPT and cyber audit reports

controls.title: Develop, communicate and enforce cybersecurity risk-management roles and authorities
controls.prose: Cybersecurity risk management roles, responsibilities and authorities shall be developed, communicated, understood and enforced.
controls.guidance: Map the roles named in the cybersecurity policy (CISO or Designated Officer, asset owners, custodians, IT Committee, SOC lead, incident manager) to named people in details.json; runtime-probe-identity-access checks that privileged roles in production IAM correspond to the documented custodians.
evidenceExpected: RACI or responsibility matrix for cybersecurity risk management
Evidence of communication (policy acknowledgement, training records)

controls.title: Appoint a CISO or Designated Officer reporting to a designated authority
controls.prose: A CISO or Designated Officer shall be appointed and report to a designated authority in the organisation. For MIIs and Qualified REs the mandatory guideline requires a senior official designated as CISO whose level, grade and standing is at least equivalent to CTO/CIO and who reports directly to the MD and CEO (reporting to an ED or MD/CEO per organisational structure is deemed compliant, FAQ Q2); MIIs and REs identified as CII shall define the CISO's role per NCIIPC guidelines. Mid-size, small-size and self-certification REs shall designate a senior official as Designated Officer. Every RE shall establish a time-bound procedure for reporting incidents and unusual activities to the CISO or Designated Officer. A group-level CISO may serve multiple group entities and a remote CISO dedicated to one organisation is permitted, but part-time CISOs holding the role at several REs are not (FAQ Q3-Q4).
controls.guidance: Record the CISO or Designated Officer, reporting line and appointment date in details.json; refresh-ctx raises a finding when the role is vacant, held part-time across unrelated REs, or (for MIIs and Qualified REs) reports below ED level. Incident records in the ledger should show the time the CISO was notified relative to detectedAt to evidence the time-bound reporting procedure.
evidenceExpected: Board resolution or appointment letter of the CISO or Designated Officer with reporting line
Organisation chart showing CISO grade equivalent to CTO/CIO for MIIs and Qualified REs
Incident escalation procedure naming the CISO and the notification time limit

controls.title: Align budgeting with information-security objectives and allocate adequate resources
controls.prose: Budgetary planning shall be aligned with information security and privacy management objectives and processes, and adequate resources shall be allocated and aligned with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles and policies. The guideline requires an adequate percentage of total IT budget to be allocated to cybersecurity under a separate budgetary head monitored by the Board or top management, with resourcing revisited regularly. CCI parameter 1 targets information security budget at 10 percent of the IT budget.
controls.guidance: Record the approved cybersecurity budget head and its share of IT budget as parameters; report-audit-improvements uses it in the KPI table when computing cost of audit against budget. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Approved budget showing a separate cybersecurity head and its share of IT budget
Board or management review of resourcing against implementation progress

params.label: Share of IT budget devoted to information security (CCI parameter 1 target)

controls.title: Access only after a signed confidentiality and integrity agreement; personnel due diligence
controls.prose: Employees and third-party service providers shall be allowed access to the RE's information systems only after they have signed a confidentiality and integrity agreement. The guideline for GV.RR.S5-S6 requires due diligence and screening of every hire, security training at onboarding and regularly, employment and termination procedures, and a signed confidentiality and integrity agreement plus due diligence for all third-party providers accessing IT systems. CCI parameter 13 measures the percentage of users granted access only after signing the agreement.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access samples active production and privileged accounts and asks HR/vendor management for the matching signed agreement; an observation records the sampled coverage. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Signed confidentiality and integrity agreements for sampled employees and third-party users
Background screening and onboarding checklist
NDA and due diligence file per third-party provider with system access

controls.title: Include cybersecurity in human resources training programmes
controls.prose: Cybersecurity shall be included in human resources training programmes, covering onboarding and regular refreshers so that every employee presents a low or no threat to the RE's cybersecurity posture.
controls.guidance: Evidence the HR onboarding curriculum and refresher schedule; the annual PR.AT.S1 training records and CCI parameter 3 (security personnel trained within the year) serve as the quantitative proof.
evidenceExpected: HR onboarding curriculum including cybersecurity modules
Attendance records for periodic refreshers

controls.title: Board-approved cybersecurity and cyber resilience policy encompassing CSCRF
controls.prose: A comprehensive cybersecurity and cyber resilience policy shall be documented and implemented after approval from the Board, partners or proprietor; it shall include industry best practices and encompass the standards and guidelines in CSCRF. The mandatory guideline requires the policy to be formulated as part of the operational risk management framework, to state reasons for any deviations from CSCRF, and to be reviewed periodically by the approving body. Supporting policies (asset, patch and vulnerability management, VAPT, audit, monitoring, configuration and change management, SSDLC, authentication and authorisation, segmentation, internet-facing asset commissioning, encryption, PII and privacy, control management, asset ownership, chain of command, and do's and don'ts for information assets) may be standalone or part of the policy; a Board-approved policy for mobile and web applications shall cover functionality, security and performance requirements; all Regulatory Data and IT and Cybersecurity Data shall be accessible to SEBI when required, with third-party agreements facilitating that; the policy shall define the Identify-Protect-Detect-Respond-Recover process; for REs identified as CII by NCIIPC the policy shall encompass NCIIPC's Guidelines for Protection of National Critical Information Infrastructure (CIR/2025/119 clause 6.8); and REs other than small-size and self-certification shall incorporate ISO 27001/27002 best practices and Plan-Do-Check-Act.
controls.guidance: Store the policy version, approval date and approving body as control-record parameters; probe-sdlc compares company-profile/<c>/sdlc/policy.json against the list of required sub-policies and raises a finding per missing area. Any recorded deviation from CSCRF must be present in the policy document with rationale, so a soc finding whose remediation is deferred by policy links to this control.
evidenceExpected: Board/partner/proprietor-approved cybersecurity and cyber resilience policy with version history
List of supporting policies mapped to the required areas
Documented deviations from CSCRF with rationale
Board-approved mobile and web application security policy

controls.title: Review the cybersecurity and cyber resilience policy annually
controls.prose: The cybersecurity and cyber resilience policy shall be reviewed periodically by the RE; Table 15 item 3 fixes the periodicity as annual for all REs, with the review performed by the Board, partners or proprietor with a view to strengthening cyber resilience.
controls.guidance: refresh-soc flags the control overdue when the policy approval date is older than the financial-year window; the review minute is the observation evidence.
evidenceExpected: Minutes of the annual policy review by the approving body
Change log between policy versions

params.label: Policy reviews per financial year

controls.title: Establish, communicate and enforce a cybersecurity risk-management policy
controls.prose: A policy for managing cybersecurity risks shall be established based on organisational context, cybersecurity strategy and priorities, and shall be communicated and enforced.
controls.guidance: The risk-management policy may be a chapter of the main policy; probe-sdlc checks that policy.json names the risk methodology, risk appetite owner and register location referenced by GV.RM.S1 and GV.RM.S4.
evidenceExpected: Cybersecurity risk-management policy or chapter with communication evidence

controls.title: Review and update the risk-management policy annually for new threats and technologies
controls.prose: The policy for managing cybersecurity risks shall be reviewed, updated, communicated and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats and technologies; Table 15 item 4 sets the periodicity as annual for all REs.
controls.guidance: Same evidence pattern as GV.PO.S2: refresh-soc dates the control from the last review minute and marks it overdue after a financial year.
evidenceExpected: Annual review record of the risk-management policy with changes driven by new threats or technologies

controls.title: Define ownership and custodianship of every asset and a chain of command for approvals
controls.prose: Clear definition of ownership and custodian of every asset and a proper chain of command for receiving approvals shall be established and followed.
controls.guidance: refresh-metastore checks that each system and dataset in sdlc/metastore.json carries an owner and custodian; probe-cicd-env and impl-change-management check that production changes and exception approvals follow the documented chain of command.
evidenceExpected: Asset inventory with owner and custodian per asset
Approval matrix or chain of command for cybersecurity decisions

controls.title: Review risk-management strategy outcomes to adjust strategy and direction
controls.prose: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes shall be reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and directions.
controls.guidance: Evidence through IT Committee or Board minutes that consider metrics such as MTTD, MTTR, MTTC, incident counts and false positive/negative rates named in the GV.RM guideline; report-audit-improvements feeds the KPI series into this review. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Minutes showing review of risk-strategy outcomes and resulting direction changes

controls.title: Review and adjust the risk-management strategy for coverage of requirements and risks
controls.prose: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organisational requirements and risks.
controls.guidance: Compare the risk register scope against the metastore system list and the applicable-instrument set; refresh-soc records an observation when critical systems or new obligations lack a corresponding risk entry. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Strategy review record showing coverage check against systems and obligations

controls.title: Evaluate cybersecurity risk-management performance
controls.prose: Organisational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed.
controls.guidance: The kpis/ series (cost of audit, coverage, time to implementation, acceptance rate, incident rate) are Maxwell's performance evidence; report-audit-improvements writes the evaluation into summary.md. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Performance metrics reviewed by the IT Committee (MTTD, MTTR, MTTC, incident counts, audit closure rates)

controls.title: Assess cyber resilience posture using the Cyber Capability Index (CCI)
controls.prose: MIIs and Qualified REs shall assess their cyber resilience posture using CCI on a periodic basis: MIIs through a third-party assessment half-yearly and Qualified REs through self-assessment annually (Table 15; FAQ Q31), submitting evidence to the reporting authority within 15 days of completion. CCI is computed from the 23 weighted parameters in Annexure-K Table 27 (for example vulnerability mitigation 18 percent, critical assets identified 9 percent, risk management 8 percent, security budget 8 percent, SOC efficacy 5 percent, automated compliance 5 percent) and rated Exceptional (91-100), Optimal (81-90), Manageable (71-80), Developing (61-70), Bare Minimum (51-60) or Fail (50 or below, or below cut-off in any domain). Scores are taken to two decimals, partial scoring is allowed, and undefined ratios take the maximum or minimum for that parameter (FAQ Q32-Q33). MIIs and Qualified REs shall strive to build an automated tool and dashboard, preferably integrated with the log aggregator, for submitting CCI and CSCRF compliance, available at cyber audit and SEBI inspection (Box Item 4; CCI parameter 23). Exempt for Mid-size REs (Table 26) and lower categories; equivalence with a primary regulator's framework may be claimed under CIR/2025/119 Part-A.
controls.guidance: Maintain the CCI score, rating band and assessment date as parameters on the control record; report-audit-findings prints the band in the regulatory posture table and refresh-soc raises a high finding when the band is Fail or when the half-yearly (MII) or annual (Qualified RE) assessment is missing. Maxwell's own ledger and kpis series are the natural feed for the automated compliance dashboard the standard asks for; probe-cicd-env can evidence that the dashboard is generated from the log aggregator rather than manually.
evidenceExpected: Annexure-K CCI report with the 23 parameter scores, weightages and final index
Third-party assessor report for MIIs; self-assessment sign-off for Qualified REs
Submission acknowledgement within 15 days of completion
Automated compliance dashboard integrated with the log aggregator

params.label: CCI assessments per financial year (2 third-party for MIIs, 1 self-assessment for Qualified REs)
CCI index score above which the RE is not rated Fail
Days after CCI completion to submit evidence

controls.title: Cyber risk-management framework agreed by stakeholders
controls.prose: REs shall prepare a cyber risk management framework to identify, assess, mitigate and monitor risks and define security processes and procedures to address them, with objectives agreed by the RE's stakeholders. The mandatory guideline for GV.RM.S1-S2 requires the framework to identify cybersecurity risk, classify business functions, processes and assets at risk, determine risk appetite, define mitigation controls, monitor their effectiveness and evaluate major changes and incidents; to consider ISO 27005 as guidance; to include risk assessment, analysis, mitigation, monitoring, compliance, communication and compensatory controls; to use metrics such as MTTD, MTTR, MTTC, incidents detected and resolved, false positives and negatives and successful attacks; to assess employee awareness (e.g. phishing test success rate); to use IT asset management to track EOL software, unpatched and unidentified devices; and to implement risk-based transaction monitoring for fraud across delivery channels.
controls.guidance: The soc ledger's risk records (rsk_) are the risk register; refresh-soc verifies each finding on a critical system links to a risk with owner, rating and treatment, and report-audit-improvements computes MTTD/MTTR from incident timestamps. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Approved cyber risk-management framework document
Risk register with likelihood, impact, treatment and owner per risk
Metrics report (MTTD, MTTR, MTTC, false positives/negatives, phishing test results)

controls.title: Include cybersecurity risk activities in enterprise risk processes
controls.prose: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes shall be included in the RE's risk management processes.
controls.guidance: Evidence that cyber risks appear in the enterprise or operational risk register reviewed by the Board risk committee; the ledger risk records should reference the enterprise risk id. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Enterprise risk register entries for cyber risks and their review minutes

controls.title: Document and periodically test scenario-based risk responses
controls.prose: Different scenarios and their respective responses shall be documented and tested on a periodic basis to check the RE's risk management plan. The mandatory guideline requires comprehensive scenario-based testing for assessing cybersecurity risks; Annexure-E gives a sample matrix for stock exchanges (DDoS, malware, application, DNS, brute force and AD attacks across pre-open, trading and closing windows) and other REs prepare their own scenarios per business model. Scenario drills differ from red teaming, must be live rather than table-top, and all scenarios must be covered within one audit period (FAQ Q68-Q70).
controls.guidance: Record each drill as an observation with the scenario, date, participants and outcome; refresh-soc checks that the set of scenarios covered in the audit period matches the documented scenario list. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Documented attack scenarios and response plans per business model
Live drill reports covering every scenario within the audit period

controls.title: Risk tolerance and appetite statements and an IT Committee-reviewed risk register
controls.prose: Risk tolerance and risk appetite statements shall be established, communicated and maintained, informed by the RE's role in critical infrastructure and sector-specific risk analysis; REs shall clearly express risk tolerance and acceptance and maintain a risk register periodically reviewed by the IT Committee for REs.
controls.guidance: Keep the approved appetite statement reference and the last IT Committee register review date as parameters; refresh-soc marks the control overdue when no review is recorded within the quarter. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Board-approved risk appetite and tolerance statement
IT Committee minutes recording review of the risk register

groups.title: Govern: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management

controls.title: Cybersecurity supply-chain risk-management strategy agreed by stakeholders
controls.prose: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management strategy or process shall be identified, established, assessed, managed and agreed to by organisational stakeholders. FAQ Q40 expects it to include proportionate third-party risk assessment and controls, SLAs and contractual obligations, and a mandate that providers follow similar or higher information-security standards. SEBI outsourcing circulars listed in Annexure-F (intermediaries 2011, depositories 2015, exchanges and clearing corporations 2017, LPCC 2020) continue to apply.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx evidences the strategy by checking every vendor file has a criticality tier, last assessment date and contractual security clauses; an absent strategy document is a finding on this control. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Approved supply-chain risk-management strategy
Vendor tiering methodology aligned to criticality

controls.title: Identify, prioritise and assess suppliers through a cyber supply-chain risk assessment
controls.prose: Suppliers and third-party service providers of information systems, components and services shall be identified, prioritised and assessed using a cyber supply chain risk assessment process; CIR/2025/119 clause 6.6 clarifies the assessment may be done in consultation with the IT Committee for REs.
controls.guidance: Each vendors/<vendor_id>.json carries the assessment date, method and rating; refresh-vendor-ctx raises a finding for any provider of a critical system without an assessment in the last year. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Supplier inventory with criticality ranking
Completed cyber supply-chain risk assessment per critical supplier with IT Committee consultation record

controls.title: Contracts with suppliers include cybersecurity and manpower-adequacy measures
controls.prose: Contracts with suppliers and third-party service providers shall include appropriate measures to meet the objectives of the RE's cybersecurity programme and supply chain risk management plan, including manpower adequacy in the cybersecurity domain. CCI parameter 16 measures the percentage of acquisition contracts with security requirements, SLA for vulnerability closure and patching, SOC integration and, for cloud, security-of-the-cloud obligations.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx records per contract whether security requirements, vulnerability-closure SLA aligned to the three-month VAPT closure, SOC log integration, SEBI audit access and, for CSPs, MeitY empanelment clauses are present. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Contract clauses on security requirements, vulnerability closure SLA, patching, SOC integration and audit access
Register of contracts with clause coverage percentage

controls.title: Monitor and review compliance of third-party providers performing critical activities
controls.prose: REs shall monitor, review and ensure compliance of third-party service providers performing critical activities on a periodic basis: half-yearly for MIIs and Qualified REs and annually for other REs (Table 15 item 10). The mandatory guideline requires MIIs and Qualified REs whose systems (IBT, back office, customer-facing applications, infrastructure) are managed by third parties to instruct them to adhere to CSCRF and obtain cyber audit certifications from them; MIIs remain responsible for cyber resilience of applications they offer over the internet (e.g. NEAT, BOLT); all REs retain responsibility, accountability and ownership of outsourced activities, must highlight critical activities handled by third parties in periodic reports to SEBI and certify compliance, and must conduct background checks, sign NDAs and obtain cybersecurity compliance from all third-party providers. REs are solely accountable for third-party breaches (FAQ Q38).
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx records the last review date and the vendor's cyber audit certificate or SOC 2/ISO evidence per critical vendor and computes the next due date from the RE's category; the periodic SEBI report's critical-activities list is generated from vendor files where criticality is critical.
evidenceExpected: Periodic review record per critical third-party provider with compliance outcome
Cyber audit certifications obtained from providers managing RE systems
NDA, background check and cybersecurity compliance confirmation per provider
List of critical activities handled by third parties in the periodic SEBI report

params.label: Reviews of third-party managed systems per financial year (2 for MIIs and Qualified REs, 1 for others)

controls.title: Software Bill of Materials for all core and critical software
controls.prose: SBOM shall be obtained for all new software procurements of core and critical activities and kept updated with every upgrade or change; where an SBOM cannot be obtained for legacy or proprietary systems, the Board, partners or proprietor shall approve the exception with proper limitation, rationale and risk-management approach. The mandatory guideline requires SBOMs for existing critical systems within 6 months of issuance of CSCRF (by 20 February 2025), SBOMs for any new critical system software or SaaS at procurement, MIIs to include SBOM in vendor empanelment criteria, and each SBOM to contain at least licence information, supplier name, all primary components with transitive dependencies and relationships, encryption used, cryptographic hashes of components, update frequency, known unknowns, access control and error-accommodation methods. The requirement applies to in-house and third-party software alike (FAQ Q35-Q37), and SBOM is a mandatory test artefact for critical-system software under PR.IP.S15.
controls.guidance: Generate CycloneDX (or SPDX) from the build pipeline for every production image and store the reference as applications/<app_id>/images/<image_id>.cdx.json; probe-cicd-env verifies an SBOM step runs on every release, probe-app-chart and runtime-probe-appcontainers reconcile deployed image digests against SBOM component hashes, and refresh-vendor-ctx records SBOM receipt for procured and SaaS products. A critical system with no SBOM and no Board-approved exception is a high finding citing sebi-cscrf-2024:GV.SC.S5 in regulatoryRefs (topic sbom; the sla-table has no sebi-cscrf-2024 row for it, so slaDueAt and slaBasis take the sla-table default for the finding's severity).
evidenceExpected: CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM per critical application and production image with component hashes and licences
Pipeline step that regenerates the SBOM on every release or upgrade
Vendor-supplied SBOM for procured software and SaaS at procurement
Board-approved exception with rationale for legacy or proprietary systems lacking an SBOM

params.label: SBOM format accepted for critical systems
Months from CSCRF issuance to obtain SBOMs for existing critical systems

controls.title: Response and recovery planning and testing conducted with third-party providers
controls.prose: Response and recovery planning and testing shall be conducted along with third-party service providers.
controls.guidance: Drill reports under RC.RP.S2-S3 must list the third-party participants (CSP, hosted-service provider, M-SOC, connectivity vendor); refresh-vendor-ctx marks critical vendors that have never participated in a drill. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Drill or resilience test reports naming participating third-party providers
Contract clauses obliging providers to join drills

controls.title: Assess and mitigate concentration risk on outsourced agencies
controls.prose: Concentration risk on outsourced agencies shall be assessed and reviewed to achieve operational resiliency. The mandatory guideline requires REs to identify third-party providers posing concentration risk, prescribe specific controls including independent audits of their systems, validate their operational resiliency, and comply with SEBI outsourcing circulars; stock exchanges and depositories shall mitigate concentration risk among their members' providers.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx counts critical systems per provider and flags any provider supporting more than one critical activity or shared across many REs (e.g. a common back-office or CSP) as a concentration risk requiring a ledger risk record with treatment. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Concentration-risk assessment naming providers supporting multiple critical services
Independent audit reports of concentrated providers and resiliency validation

controls.title: Third-party providers mandated to follow similar information-security standards
controls.prose: Third-party service providers shall also be mandated to follow similar standards of information security to those the RE applies.
controls.guidance: Evidence is a flow-down clause in each contract and the provider's own certification (ISO 27001 for outsourced PDC/DR/SOC per PR.IP.S16 guideline, FAQ Q58); refresh-vendor-ctx records the certification scope and expiry per provider.
evidenceExpected: Flow-down security clauses in provider contracts
Provider certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2) with scope covering the outsourced service

controls.title: Time-bound inventory of physical, digital, cloud and interfacing assets
controls.prose: Physical devices, digital assets (URLs, domain names, applications, APIs), shared resources including cloud assets and other interfacing systems within the organisation shall be inventoried in a time-bound manner. The mandatory guideline for ID.AM.S1 and S4 requires all REs to maintain an up-to-date inventory of hardware, software, digital assets, cloud assets, internal and external interfacing systems, network resources, connections and data flows; to reflect any addition, deletion or change within 3 working days; to conduct criticality assessment through inventory, threat modelling and vulnerability assessment; and to maintain an up-to-date organisation-level network architecture diagram covering wired and wireless networks. MIIs shall additionally adopt a configuration management database approach. Smaller REs with minimal IT may keep manual inventories and multiple tools are permitted provided the inventory is comprehensive and current (FAQ Q9, Q11).
controls.guidance: sdlc/metastore.json is the inventory of record; refresh-metastore reconciles it against probe-iac (cloud resources), probe-app-chart (deployed workloads), runtime-probe-network-perimeter (exposed domains and IPs) and runtime-probe-prod-env (hosts) and raises a finding per unmanaged asset or per asset whose inventory timestamp lags its creation by more than the inventoryUpdateWorkingDays parameter (3 working days, per the ID.AM.S1/S4 guideline clause 'within 3 working days'; count working days, not calendar days). This is an inventory-update window, not a remediation deadline, so the control has no slaDays and remediation dueAt comes from the sla-table defaults by severity. Store the network diagram reference and its last update date as parameters.
evidenceExpected: Asset inventory (ITSM or equivalent) covering hardware, software, URLs, domains, APIs, cloud assets and interfaces with timestamps
Reconciliation of inventory against cloud, cluster and network discovery
Current organisation-level network architecture diagram

params.label: Working days within which asset changes must appear in the inventory

controls.title: Map and inventory communication, data flows and encryption methods
controls.prose: Organisational communication, data flows and encryption methods shall be mapped and inventoried with respect to all IT systems and network resources. Box Item 7 and FAQ Q13 extend this to a comprehensive inventory of cryptographic assets (keys, certificates, algorithms, what cryptography each application uses and for what purpose) prioritised for post-quantum cryptography migration.
controls.guidance: refresh-metastore records data flows and the transport and at-rest encryption per flow in metastore.json; probe-schemas and runtime-probe-datapipeline evidence the encryption on each pipeline hop and probe-iac the TLS versions, KMS keys and certificate inventory. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Data-flow diagrams per critical system with encryption method per flow
Cryptographic asset inventory (keys, certificates, algorithms, owners) with PQC migration priority

controls.title: No shadow IT assets
controls.prose: REs shall ensure that no shadow IT assets are present in the organisation.
controls.guidance: Any asset discovered by probe-iac, probe-app-chart, runtime-probe-network-perimeter, runtime-probe-harnesses or runtime-probe-sandboxes that is absent from metastore.json is recorded as a shadow-IT finding on this control; agent harnesses and sandboxes are a common source and probe-agent-graph lists tools and MCP servers not in the inventory.
evidenceExpected: Discovery scan results reconciled to the inventory with zero unmanaged assets
Process for approving new SaaS, cloud accounts and developer tooling

controls.title: Board-approved list of critical systems per the CSCRF definition
controls.prose: The Board, partners or proprietor shall approve the list of critical systems. Critical systems (on premise and cloud) include any system whose compromise adversely impacts core and critical business operations, systems storing or transmitting data required by regulation, devices and networks through which critical systems connect, internet-facing and client-facing systems, and, per CIR/2025/119 clause 6.1, any other system on the same network segment as those systems (replacing the earlier ancillary-systems wording). Internet-facing but non-critical tools such as survey forms may be classified by the RE on risk assessment (FAQ Q10), and classification of connected systems considers impact, data sensitivity and connectivity (FAQ Q12). CCI parameter 19 targets critical systems at 50 percent of systems integrated with SOC.
controls.guidance: metastore.json flags each system critical with the applicable definition clause and the approval reference; refresh-metastore raises a finding when an internet-facing, client-facing or regulated-data system is not flagged critical, and runtime-probe-network-perimeter identifies systems sharing a network segment with critical ones. The critical list drives 100 percent audit and VAPT coverage under Sec-4.3 and Sec-4.4.
evidenceExpected: Board/partner/proprietor-approved list of critical systems with classification rationale
Network segment mapping showing systems co-located with critical systems

controls.title: Inventories of data and metadata for designated data types
controls.prose: Inventories of data, and corresponding metadata for designated data types, are maintained.
controls.guidance: probe-schemas catalogues datasets and their schemas into metastore.json with classification (Regulatory Data or IT and Cybersecurity Data per PR.DS.S2), PII flags and retention; datasets found in runtime-probe-datapipeline without a metastore entry are findings on this control.
evidenceExpected: Data inventory with classification, owner, location and retention per dataset
Schema catalogue reconciled to production data stores

controls.title: Manage all inventoried assets and data through their lifecycle in an ITSM tool
controls.prose: All inventoried IT assets and data are managed throughout their lifecycles; the mandatory guideline requires all IT assets to be inventoried in an ITSM tool and cybersecurity considerations to be integrated into product life cycles. Under CIR/2025/119 Part-A this ITSM requirement is one where equivalence with a primary regulator's framework may be claimed.
controls.guidance: Record the ITSM tool and its coverage as parameters; probe-sdlc evidences that product life cycles include security gates and refresh-metastore checks commissioning and decommissioning dates per asset. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: ITSM tool export showing lifecycle status per asset
Product life-cycle procedure with security checkpoints

controls.title: Identify, validate and document asset vulnerabilities and risk factors
controls.prose: Asset vulnerabilities shall be identified, validated and documented, and risk factors shall be assessed and managed for all IT assets of the RE. The mandatory guideline requires the risk assessment to cover the technology stack, known vulnerabilities, third-party dependence, data storage, security and privacy, and threats and likelihoods, and to yield a quantifiable cybersecurity risk score.
controls.guidance: Vulnerability findings from VAPT, scanners, cves/ records and probe workflows are the ledger evidence; refresh-soc links each to a risk and CVSS-derived severity. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Vulnerability register with validation status per asset
Quantified risk score methodology and latest result

controls.title: Periodic risk assessment of the IT environment including post-quantum risks
controls.prose: Risk assessment (including post-quantum risks) of the RE's IT environment shall be done on a periodic basis: half-yearly for MIIs and yearly for Qualified and Mid-size REs (Table 15 item 6), to obtain visibility of the overall risk posture and a quantifiable cybersecurity risk score. Box Item 7 sets out indicative measures for quantum readiness: inventory of cryptographic assets prioritised for PQC migration, strategies for assets that can and cannot migrate, skills, policy revision and proof-of-concept trials, feasibility of PQC and QKD, monitoring of quantum developments, and crypto-agility. CCI parameter 15 measures the share of systems covered by risk assessment.
controls.guidance: Record the assessment date, scope coverage percentage and risk score as parameters; refresh-soc marks the control overdue by category cadence. probe-iac and probe-schemas evidence the cryptographic inventory (algorithms, key sizes, TLS versions) used for the PQC prioritisation. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Risk assessment report with scope, methodology and quantified score for the period
Cryptographic asset inventory with PQC migration priorities
IT Committee review of the assessment

params.label: Threat-based risk assessments per financial year (2 for MIIs, 1 for Qualified and Mid-size REs)

controls.title: Receive and act on cyber threat intelligence and CERT-In/CSIRT-Fin advisories within 24 hours
controls.prose: REs shall receive CTI from reliable and trusted forums, be on-boarded to the CERT-In intelligence platform, and implement advisories issued by CERT-In and CSIRT-Fin in a timely manner, which footnote 19 defines as within 24 hours of receipt or as indicated by SEBI. The mandatory guideline for MIIs and Qualified REs adds dark-web monitoring and takedown services, anti-phishing and anti-rogue-app subscriptions, SOPs for implementing government advisories within a defined timeframe, and processes to ingest IOAs, IOCs, malware and vulnerability alerts; MIIs shall also on-board to NCCC. REs are encouraged to supplement NCIIPC and CERT-In feeds with industry and commercial sources (FAQ Q67). Exempt for Mid-size REs (Table 26) and lower categories.
controls.guidance: Maintain an advisory log with receipt time and implementation or risk-acceptance time; refresh-soc raises a finding when an advisory relevant to a component in the SBOM inventory or cves/ data is open past 24 hours. runtime-probe-network-perimeter evidences blocking of advisory-listed malicious domains and IPs.
evidenceExpected: CERT-In intelligence platform onboarding confirmation (and NCCC for MIIs)
Advisory log with receipt and implementation timestamps
Dark-web monitoring, takedown and anti-phishing service contracts and reports

params.label: Hours to implement CERT-In/CSIRT-Fin advisories after receipt

controls.title: Use threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood and impact to prioritise risk response; monitor phishing domains
controls.prose: Threats, vulnerabilities, their likelihoods and impacts shall be used to understand inherent risk and develop risk response prioritisation, with vulnerabilities and threats related to access and authentication identified and documented. The mandatory guideline requires all REs to proactively monitor cyberspace for phishing websites using the RE's domains and report them to CSIRT-Fin/CERT-In, and recommends risk-based authentication that analyses device, location, network and sensitivity at every login.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter checks look-alike domain registrations and certificate-transparency logs for the RE's brands and records phishing takedown requests; runtime-probe-identity-access evidences RBA policies on customer and staff identity providers.
evidenceExpected: Risk prioritisation methodology using likelihood and impact
Phishing domain monitoring reports and CERT-In/CSIRT-Fin takedown requests
Risk-based authentication configuration on login flows

controls.title: Choose, prioritise, plan, track and communicate risk responses
controls.prose: Risk responses shall be chosen, prioritised, planned, tracked and communicated.
controls.guidance: Ledger risk records carry treatment (treat, tolerate, terminate, transfer), owner and due date and link to initiatives in change_management/master.json; impl-change-management tracks execution and report-audit-improvements reports time to implementation. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
evidenceExpected: Risk treatment plan with owners and target dates
Tracking of treatment progress reported to the IT Committee

groups.title: Protect: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

controls.title: Issue, manage, verify, revoke and audit identities and credentials
controls.prose: Identities and credentials are issued, managed, verified, revoked and audited for authorised devices, users and processes. The mandatory guideline requires that no person has an intrinsic right of access by rank; access is for a defined purpose and period on need-to-use and least-privilege basis with effective authentication; access to external cloud storage (Dropbox, Google Drive, iCloud, OneDrive) is governed by policy; account lock-out after failed attempts applies to all accounts; existing accounts are periodically reviewed by system owners for dormant, over-privileged or unknown accounts; and end-of-life procedures deactivate named, default and generic IDs of leavers. Stock brokers providing algorithmic trading shall isolate and secure the perimeter and connectivity of algo servers.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access lists identities in the IdP, cloud IAM and databases, compares them against HR leavers and vendor rosters, checks lock-out policies and reports dormant or generic accounts; probe-iac evidences IAM-as-code and runtime-probe-network-perimeter the algo-server segmentation for brokers.
evidenceExpected: Joiner-mover-leaver process with deprovisioning evidence for sampled leavers
Account lock-out policy settings per system
Periodic account review by system owners with dormant-account clean-up
For algo brokers, network isolation of algorithmic trading servers

controls.title: Protect network integrity through segregation and segmentation
controls.prose: Network integrity is protected through measures such as network segregation and segmentation. The mandatory guideline (all REs except small-size and self-certification) requires segmentation and isolation with segment-to-segment access on least privilege; WAF, proxy and IPS in front of internet-exposed infrastructure; web and email filters blocking known bad domains and malicious indicators with antivirus scanning at host and gateway; whitelist-based configuration of IPs, ports and services with ACLs; DNS filtering and DNSSEC; management of critical servers only from enterprise intranet systems; SPF, DMARC and DKIM; email protection best practices; blocking of CSIRT-Fin/CERT-In listed malicious domains and IPs; and a centralised inventory of authorised devices with automated discovery. All REs must deploy anti-malware and ransomware controls with regular signature updates, baseline configuration standards for OS, databases, network and mobile devices with enforcement checks, secured LAN and wireless access, and limited SMTP connections.
controls.guidance: probe-iac reads security groups, NACLs, VPC/VNet peering and firewall rules for default-deny and whitelist patterns; runtime-probe-network-perimeter tests exposed services, WAF presence, DNS filtering, DNSSEC, SPF/DMARC/DKIM records and mail-gateway scanning; probe-app-chart checks Kubernetes NetworkPolicies between namespaces hosting critical workloads. Small-size and self-certification REs are bound only by the all-RE sub-guidelines.
evidenceExpected: Network segmentation design with segment-to-segment access rules
Firewall and cloud security-group rules showing whitelist-based inbound and outbound control
WAF, IPS, proxy, DNS filtering and email gateway configurations
SPF, DMARC and DKIM records for all sending domains
Baseline configuration standards with enforcement check results

controls.title: Least privilege and segregation of duties for on-premise and cloud permissions
controls.prose: While granting access permissions and authorisations to resources, both on premise and cloud, the Principle of Least Privilege shall be followed along with segregation of duties. The guideline requires a PIM solution or process to track privileged access, strong password controls (Annexure-G), an internet access policy for critical infrastructure, and supervision of privileged staff including limiting their number, periodic review of their activities, preventing privileged users from accessing logs of their own activity, and strong controls over their remote access. CCI parameter 8 targets 100 percent of privileged access through PIM.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access enumerates privileged roles in cloud IAM, Kubernetes RBAC, databases and the IdP, checks for wildcard policies and shared admin accounts, and confirms a PAM/PIM broker fronts privileged sessions; probe-iac flags overly broad IAM policies in code and probe-cicd-env checks that deploy credentials are scoped per environment.
evidenceExpected: Privileged account inventory with PIM/PAM coverage percentage
IAM policy review showing least privilege and segregation between development, deployment and operations
Log-access restriction preventing privileged users from editing their own audit trail

params.label: Share of privileged access brokered through PIM (CCI parameter 8 target)

controls.title: Zero Trust model for individuals, devices and resources
controls.prose: REs shall follow a Zero Trust model to allow individuals, devices and resources to access the organisation's resources. The original guideline for MIIs and Qualified REs (deny by default, allow only after authentication and authorisation) was reworded by CIR/2025/119 clause 6.2: REs shall implement suggested strategies and methodologies such as zero-trust networks, segmentation, no single point of failure and high availability, approved by the IT Committee for REs. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: Evidence the IT Committee-approved zero-trust roadmap; runtime-probe-identity-access checks device posture and conditional-access policies for access to critical systems, runtime-probe-network-perimeter checks that no critical service is reachable without authentication, and probe-app-chart checks service-mesh mTLS and NetworkPolicy default-deny for critical namespaces.
evidenceExpected: IT Committee-approved zero-trust, segmentation and high-availability strategy
Conditional access and device posture policies for critical systems
Default-deny network policies and mutual TLS between services

controls.title: Periodic access-rights review with maker-checker for rights changes
controls.prose: Access rights shall be reviewed and documented on a periodic basis and a maker-checker framework shall be implemented for granting, revoking and modifying user rights in applications, databases and other systems. User access rights, delegated access and unused tokens shall be reviewed quarterly by MIIs and Qualified REs and half-yearly by other REs (Table 15 item 7); MIIs and Qualified REs shall clean delegated access and unused tokens at least quarterly.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access exports access-review campaigns from the IdP and cloud IAM (last completed date, reviewers, revocations), lists API tokens and service-account keys older than the review window, and checks that IAM changes in probe-iac or ticketing show a second approver; refresh-soc computes the next due review by category.
evidenceExpected: Completed access review campaign per system with revocations actioned
Inventory of tokens and delegated access with age and last-use
Maker-checker approval trail for rights changes

params.label: User access, delegated access and token reviews per financial year (4 for MIIs and Qualified REs, 2 for others)

controls.title: Comprehensive authentication policy with identity proofing and risk-commensurate factors
controls.prose: A comprehensive authentication policy shall be documented and implemented; identities shall be proofed, bound to credentials and asserted in interactions, and users, devices and assets authenticated (single or multi-factor) commensurate with transaction risk. The mandatory guideline requires defined password complexity, removal of unused generic user and email IDs, and for REs other than small-size and self-certification, password controls covering change on first login, minimum length and history, complexity and maximum validity, with credential data stored using strong hashing algorithms (Annexure-G suggests bcrypt or PBKDF2 and warns against forced frequent rotation for customers).
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access reads IdP and directory password and lock-out policies and checks generic accounts; execute-scr inspects authentication code paths for hashing algorithm and salt handling; probe-schemas checks credential columns are hashed not encrypted or plain. Customer-facing IBT/SWST flows require at least two factors (Annexure-G item 3).
evidenceExpected: Authentication policy with password parameters and identity proofing procedure
Directory and IdP policy screenshots or exports for complexity, history, validity and first-login change
Code or configuration showing bcrypt/PBKDF2/Argon2 password hashing

params.label: Minimum password length (organisation-set; CSCRF requires a reasonable minimum without stating a number)
Hashing algorithm for stored credentials

controls.title: MFA on all critical systems for access from untrusted to trusted networks
controls.prose: All critical systems shall have MFA implemented for all users accessing from an untrusted network to a trusted network. The guideline requires multi-factor security (VPN, firewall controls) and MFA on all internet-accessible critical systems, and MFA for all users and systems connecting online, particularly VPNs, webmail and accounts reaching critical systems from non-trusted environments. CCI parameter 4 targets 100 percent of remote users through MFA.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access checks MFA enforcement on the IdP, VPN, cloud console, bastions, webmail and CI/CD for every account, listing exceptions; runtime-probe-network-perimeter confirms no critical service accepts single-factor logins from the internet; probe-agent-graph checks agent harness consoles and MCP endpoints reachable remotely also require MFA. A single privileged account without MFA on a critical system is a high finding citing sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S7 in regulatoryRefs (topic mfa; the sla-table has no sebi-cscrf-2024 row for it, so slaDueAt and slaBasis take the sla-table default for the finding's severity).
evidenceExpected: MFA enforcement report per identity provider, VPN and cloud console with zero exceptions for critical systems
Remote-access log sample showing MFA challenge for every session

params.label: Share of remote users authenticating through MFA (CCI parameter 4 target)

controls.title: Documented log-management policy covering all log sources
controls.prose: A comprehensive log management policy shall be documented and implemented. The mandatory guideline advises identifying all log sources and collecting system, application, network, database, security, performance, audit-trail and event logs; a strong retention policy per SEBI/GoI requirements including the IT Act, the DPDP Act and CERT-In/NCIIPC directions; monitoring of all event and incident logs for unusual patterns; and secure handling when sharing logs (FAQ Q54). CIR/2025/119 Table 1 places log management under the principle of exclusivity for multi-regulated REs.
controls.guidance: probe-app-chart and probe-iac evidence that every critical workload, database, load balancer and cloud account ships logs to the SIEM; runtime-probe-prod-env and runtime-probe-datapipeline sample log sources on hosts and pipelines and compare against the SOC's Annexure-N Table 29 source list; probe-agent-graph confirms agent harness and tool-call logs are included. Missing log sources feed the SOC efficacy metric under DE.CM.S3.
evidenceExpected: Log management policy naming log types, sources, retention and monitoring responsibilities
Log-source inventory reconciled to SIEM ingestion
Retention configuration per log store

controls.title: Uniquely identified user logs for critical systems retained at least two years
controls.prose: User logs shall be uniquely identified and stored for a specified period. The mandatory guideline requires records of user access to critical systems to be uniquely identified and logged for audit, maintained in a secure location for not less than two years (at least 6 months online and the rest in archival mode), with records of users having access to shared accounts. CERT-In Direction (iv) separately requires 180 days of ICT logs within India and DPDP Rule 6(1)(e) one year for personal-data processing logs; the CSCRF two-year period is the binding minimum for critical-system access logs.
controls.guidance: probe-iac reads retention on log buckets, SIEM hot/cold tiers and database audit settings; runtime-probe-prod-env confirms 6 months are queryable online and archives exist to 24 months; runtime-probe-datapipeline checks log pipelines do not drop user identifiers. Record the configured online and archival retention as parameters and raise a finding citing sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S9 in regulatoryRefs (topic log-retention; the sla-table has no sebi-cscrf-2024 row for it, so slaDueAt and slaBasis take the sla-table default for the finding's severity) when either is below the default.
evidenceExpected: Retention configuration showing 6 months online and 24 months total for critical-system access logs
Sample log entries with unique user identifiers for shared-account use
Archive integrity and restore test for aged logs

params.label: Minimum retention of critical-system user access logs
Minimum online (searchable) retention before archival

controls.title: Managed, monitored and recorded physical access; personnel screening
controls.prose: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored and protected; physical access to critical systems shall be monitored and recorded continuously, and individuals shall be screened before being granted access to organisational information and systems. The mandatory guideline restricts physical access to critical systems to authorised officials with third parties escorted, revokes access immediately when no longer required, and secures critical equipment rooms with guards, CCTV, card access, mantraps or bollards. CCI parameters 12 and 14 measure unauthorised physical entries (target 0 percent) and screened individuals (target 100 percent).
controls.guidance: For colocation, PDC and DR sites evidence the provider's access logs and CCTV retention; for cloud, the CSP's audit reports cover physical security and refresh-vendor-ctx records them. Screening evidence is sampled with GV.RR.S5.
evidenceExpected: Physical access logs and CCTV retention for rooms hosting critical systems
Escort procedure and visitor register for third parties
Pre-employment screening records

controls.title: Periodic review of privileged users' activities and time-bound third-party access
controls.prose: Privileged users' activities shall be reviewed periodically (quarterly for MIIs and Qualified REs, half-yearly for other REs, Table 15 item 8); access restrictions apply to employees and third-party providers, and any access granted shall be for a limited period on need-to-know basis under stringent supervision and monitoring. The remote-support guideline (all REs except small-size and self-certification) requires OEM and integrator remote support to be governed, logged and audited, RDP used only on need-to-use basis with MFA from whitelisted IPs for a predefined period with full activity logging, stringent supervision of third parties on critical systems, and monitoring of environmental controls, availability alerts and access logs.
