controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access exports PAM session recordings and privileged-activity review sign-offs, checks vendor accounts have expiry dates and that RDP/SSH bastions enforce MFA and IP allow-lists; refresh-soc computes the next review date by category.
evidenceExpected: Privileged activity review sign-off per period with anomalies actioned
Vendor and remote-support access register with time limits, whitelisted IPs and MFA
PAM session logs for sampled privileged sessions

params.label: Privileged users' activity reviews per financial year (4 for MIIs and Qualified REs, 2 for others)

controls.title: Strictly tracked and administered remote access
controls.prose: Remote access to assets shall be strictly tracked and administered. CCI parameter 4 requires an automated record of all remote access points, IDS/IPS monitoring of remote traffic, review of remote access logs and MFA for every remote user.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter enumerates VPN concentrators, bastions, zero-trust proxies and any directly exposed RDP/SSH/database ports and compares them with the approved remote access point inventory; runtime-probe-identity-access checks per-user MFA and session logging on each.
evidenceExpected: Inventory of remote access points with owner and monitoring coverage
VPN/bastion session logs with user, source IP, MFA result and duration
External scan showing no unapproved remote-access ports

controls.title: Documented data-disposal and data-retention policy
controls.prose: A comprehensive data-disposal and data-retention policy shall be documented and implemented to identify the value and lifetime of various parcels of data.
controls.guidance: probe-schemas records retention per dataset in metastore.json and compares against the policy; probe-iac checks lifecycle rules on object storage and database backup retention; runtime-probe-datapipeline verifies purge jobs run. Align retention with DPDP Rule 8 erasure and PR.AA.S9 log minimums.
evidenceExpected: Data retention and disposal policy with retention periods per data class
Storage lifecycle rules and purge job evidence matching the policy

controls.title: SOPs for handling and disposing of storage media
controls.prose: Comprehensive SOPs shall be documented for handling storage media devices and their disposal; critical data on such devices shall be removed by wiping, overwriting, degaussing, crypto-shredding or physical destruction as applicable. CCI parameter 11 targets 100 percent of disposed media passing sanitisation testing.
controls.guidance: Evidence the SOP, disposal certificates and, for cloud, the CSP's media sanitisation attestation captured by refresh-vendor-ctx; probe-iac checks that encrypted volumes and buckets use customer-managed keys so crypto-shredding is possible.
evidenceExpected: Media handling and disposal SOP
Disposal and sanitisation certificates per decommissioned device
CSP attestation of media sanitisation for cloud storage

controls.title: Access control for endpoints, networks, APIs, removable media, laptops and mobiles
controls.prose: Access control for endpoint devices, networks, APIs, removable media, laptops, mobiles and similar systems shall be defined and implemented. The mandatory guideline (all REs except small-size and self-certification) requires EPP/EDR/XDR and anti-malware on endpoints with updated signatures, IPS/NG-IPS network monitoring, PowerShell and local admin rights disabled by default, regular Active Directory review and penetration testing for DC abuse, and a policy restricting and securely erasing removable media and electronic devices. MIIs shall additionally secure domain controllers: patch on release with quarterly review, no unnecessary software, access limited to a small Administrators group with separate day-to-day accounts, and host firewalls preventing direct internet access. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-prod-env and runtime-probe-devtest-env sample hosts for EDR agent presence and version, local admin membership and PowerShell execution policy; runtime-probe-identity-access reviews AD privileged groups and service accounts; runtime-probe-sandboxes and runtime-probe-harnesses check that agent execution environments also run endpoint protection and restrict shell access.
evidenceExpected: EDR/EPP coverage report across servers and endpoints with signature currency
Group policy or MDM settings disabling local admin and PowerShell by default
AD review and DC penetration test reports
Removable media policy and enforcement logs

controls.title: Mobile applications vetted against security requirements and tested before deployment
controls.prose: Mobile applications shall be properly vetted against security requirements and thoroughly tested before deployment. The detailed mobile application security guidelines (root and emulator detection, device-policy enforcement, unsecured-network detection, anti-malware and overlay protection, anti-tampering with runtime signature validation, published checksums, remote-access and screen-mirroring detection, re-authentication after inactivity, no sensitive data stored on device, protection against injection, encrypted sensitive writes, device binding to device, number and SIM, OWASP MASVS, and containerised business apps) were declared recommendatory rather than mandatory by CIR/2025/119 clause 6.3; the standard itself remains and FAQ Q57 points to it for baseline requirements. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: probe-sdlc and probe-cicd-env evidence a mobile app security test stage (MASVS-based SAST/DAST) before store release and published checksums; execute-scr reviews root-detection, secure storage and certificate-pinning code; VA and PT of mobile applications is a mandatory item of the Annexure-L VAPT scope regardless of the guideline's status.
evidenceExpected: Mobile application security test report (MASVS) per release
Published checksums for released APK/IPA builds
Release gate evidence that testing completed before store submission

controls.title: API security with authentication, authorisation, rate limiting and whitelisting
controls.prose: API security with proper authentication and authorisation mechanisms shall be defined and implemented. The mandatory guideline (all REs except small-size and self-certification) requires rate limiting and throttling, access management so only intended entities reach APIs, adherence to OWASP API development documentation with the OWASP API Top 10 mitigated, and whitelist-based connectivity; where MIIs provide APIs consumed by REs the onus of API security is on the MII, which shall deploy API security solutions. MIIs and Qualified REs shall also prepare SOPs for open-source application security and emerging-technology concerns such as Generative AI security. Application security testing under PR.IP.S15 must include API security and discovery. Exempt for small-size and self-certification REs on-boarded to Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: probe-app-chart and probe-iac evidence gateway policies (authentication, rate limits, IP allow-lists) per exposed API; runtime-probe-network-perimeter discovers undocumented APIs and tests unauthenticated access; execute-scr checks authorisation at object level; probe-agent-graph and runtime-probe-harnesses evidence the GenAI security SOP by checking tool permissions, prompt-injection controls and egress restrictions of agent harnesses, mapping to owasp-llm-top10-2025 and owasp-agentic-top10-2026.
evidenceExpected: API inventory with authentication scheme, rate limit and consumer allow-list per API
API gateway or WAF policy exports
API security test results covering OWASP API Top 10
SOP for open-source and Generative AI application security (MIIs and Qualified REs)

controls.title: Mandatory periodic cybersecurity, cyber resilience and system hygiene awareness programmes
controls.prose: Mandatory programmes for building awareness of cybersecurity, cyber resilience and system hygiene among employees shall be established, conducted periodically and updated as new threats, technologies and industry trends emerge. The mandatory guidelines for all REs require a focus on employees from non-technical disciplines, awareness of social engineering and phishing, security awareness campaigns stressing avoidance of clicking links and attachments in email (CERT-In and CSIRT-Fin advisories may be used), periodic training on IT and cybersecurity policy updated for current threats and extended where possible to outsourced staff and third-party service providers, and periodic review of training content. CSCRF Table 15 fixes training at least annually.
controls.guidance: Evidence the training calendar, completion percentages and phishing-simulation results for the financial year; refresh-soc raises a finding when completion for staff with access to critical systems is incomplete at financial-year end or when content was not revised in the year. report-audit-improvements tracks completion trend. Maxwell does not observe training directly, so the control record relies on LMS exports attached as evidence.
evidenceExpected: Board or IT Committee approved awareness programme and training calendar
LMS completion report by employee, outsourced staff and third-party personnel
Phishing simulation campaign results and follow-up training
Record of annual content review

params.label: Minimum cybersecurity training cycles per financial year

controls.title: Privileged users understand their roles and responsibilities
controls.prose: REs shall ensure that privileged users understand their roles and responsibilities; the shared mandatory guideline for PR.AT.S1-S2 requires periodic training on IT and cybersecurity policy and current threats for these users.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access enumerates privileged identities (cloud admin roles, cluster-admin bindings, database superusers, PAM vault users) and refresh-soc joins the list to training evidence; every privileged identity whose owner lacks role-specific training in the financial year is a finding.
evidenceExpected: List of privileged users reconciled against role-based training completion
Signed acknowledgement of privileged-user responsibilities

controls.title: Third-party stakeholders and customers understand their roles; investor grievance and fraud-reporting features
controls.prose: REs shall ensure that third-party stakeholders such as suppliers, customers or investors and partners understand their roles and responsibilities. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires mobile and web applications to carry a section with the process, forms and contacts for lodging technology and cybersecurity grievances with defined dispute-handling timelines; access to mobile and web applications only at the customer's written or authenticated electronic request with acknowledgement of terms; a mechanism in the application for authenticated customers to mark a transaction as fraudulent with immediate notification; ongoing customer awareness of cyber risks; encouragement to report phishing mails and sites with effective remedial action; and education on the risk of sharing credentials, passwords or OTPs.
controls.guidance: execute-scr and probe-app-chart inspect customer-facing applications for the grievance section, the fraud-marking endpoint and the terms-acceptance flow before account activation; runtime-probe-qa-env exercises the flow read-only in QA. Supplier responsibility acknowledgements are recorded in vendors/<vendor_id>.json by refresh-vendor-ctx.
evidenceExpected: Screenshots or test evidence of the in-app grievance and fraud-reporting features
Customer awareness communications and phishing-report handling log
Supplier contract clauses or acknowledgements of cybersecurity responsibilities

controls.title: Senior executives and Board members understand their roles; dedicated Board programme
controls.prose: REs shall ensure that senior executives and Board members understand their roles and responsibilities, and a dedicated programme on cybersecurity, cyber resilience and system hygiene shall be made for Board members.
controls.guidance: Attach the Board programme agenda and attendance as evidence; refresh-soc raises a finding when no Board session took place in the financial year. Governance contacts in details.json identify the Board liaison to request evidence from.
evidenceExpected: Board cybersecurity programme agenda, materials and attendance
Minutes recording Board discussion of cyber resilience responsibilities

controls.title: Physical and information security personnel understand their roles
controls.prose: REs shall ensure that physical security and information security personnel understand their roles and responsibilities.
controls.guidance: Evidence role descriptions and role-specific training for SOC analysts, security engineers and physical security staff; refresh-soc raises a finding when a SOC or security role has no documented responsibilities or training in the year.
evidenceExpected: Role descriptions for information security and physical security staff
Role-specific training records

controls.title: Protect data at rest and in transit with industry-standard encryption; DLP and storage-device control
controls.prose: Data at rest and data in transit shall be protected by strong data-protection measures using industry-standard encryption algorithms, and MIIs shall also explore encrypting data in use. The mandatory guideline for PR.DS.S1-S3 (all REs except Small-size and Self-certification) requires encryption in motion, at rest and in use (data-in-use encryption for cloud deployments per the SEBI cloud framework), layering of full-disk and file-based encryption where possible, industry-standard algorithms such as RSA and AES, deployment of DLP solutions or processes, measures against unauthorised access, copying or transmission of data held in a contractual or fiduciary capacity including during exchange with external parties, an information security policy covering phones, photocopiers and scanners, and permitting only authorised storage devices. Application security for internet-facing customer applications (internet-based trading, portals and back-office applications) follows the illustrative measures of Annexure-G (all REs except Self-certification). CIR/2025/60 clause 5 makes a dedicated HSM mandatory for MIIs and Qualified REs under the cloud framework, while other categories may use a Board-approved risk-assessed alternative. Exempt for Small-size and Self-certification REs on Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks encryption-at-rest settings on storage, databases, snapshots and KMS key policies (and HSM-backed keys for MIIs and Qualified REs); runtime-probe-network-perimeter verifies TLS versions and ciphers on exposed endpoints; runtime-probe-datapipeline verifies encryption on internal transfer hops and SFTP or API exchanges with external parties; probe-app-chart checks service-to-service mTLS and secret mounting. Each unencrypted store or plaintext hop carrying regulatory data is a high finding citing sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S1 in regulatoryRefs (topic encryption; the sla-table has no sebi-cscrf-2024 row for it, so slaDueAt and slaBasis take the sla-table default for the finding's severity).
evidenceExpected: Encryption configuration for storage, databases, backups and key management (HSM for MIIs and Qualified REs)
TLS scan results for internet-facing and internal endpoints
DLP policy and alert reports
Policy covering removable media, phones, scanners and authorised storage devices

params.label: Dedicated HSM mandatory for key management (MIIs and Qualified REs, CIR/2025/60 clause 5)

controls.title: Classify data into Regulatory Data and IT and Cybersecurity Data; data localisation (in abeyance)
controls.prose: REs shall classify their data into Regulatory Data (data of core and critical activities, investor communications, data required by SEBI or Government of India, and data deemed sensitive) and IT and Cybersecurity Data (logs and metadata that contain no Regulatory Data or sensitive architecture, vulnerability, privileged-user, password-hash or configuration details, and from which Regulatory Data cannot ordinarily be generated) (Box Item 9). As published, the standard requires Regulatory Data to be kept available and easily accessible in legible and usable form within the legal boundaries of India, including original data of investors incorporated outside India, with an application to read retained data where it is not in readable form; IT and Cybersecurity Data sent to global SOCs or SaaS cybersecurity solutions is exempt, but must be classified, assessed and reviewed at least annually by the IT Committee, approved annually by the Board, partners or proprietor, and made available to SEBI, CERT-In or any government agency within 48 hours of request; classification must follow the IT Act 2000 and DPDP Act 2023 (Box Item 10; PR.DS.S1-S3 guideline). CIR/2024/184 clause 2.3 has kept the data localisation guidelines and provisions of PR.DS.S2 in abeyance until further notification, and CIR/2025/119 Part-A lists data classification and localisation under the principle of exclusivity. FAQ Q26 (June 2025) nonetheless states that encryption keys and key-management operations for cloud workloads must remain within India and that SEBI is consulting on final localisation guidelines.
controls.guidance: Treat localisation gaps as observations, not findings, while the abeyance stands: probe-iac and refresh-metastore record the region of every store holding Regulatory Data and every cross-border log or SIEM export, and runtime-probe-datapipeline records egress destinations, so the posture is ready when SEBI re-notifies. The data classification inventory itself is still expected in sdlc/metastore.json. Needs maintainer verification: confirm on the SEBI circulars page whether the CIR/2024/184 abeyance has been lifted or replaced before raising this control to mandatory.
evidenceExpected: Data classification register tagging Regulatory Data and IT and Cybersecurity Data per store and flow
Region inventory of stores holding Regulatory Data
IT Committee review and Board approval of IT and Cybersecurity Data sent to offshore SOC or SaaS tools
KMS or HSM region evidence showing key operations within India

params.label: Hours within which offshore IT and Cybersecurity Data must be produced to SEBI, CERT-In or a government agency
Minimum IT Committee reviews per year of IT and Cybersecurity Data sent offshore

controls.title: Maintain adequate capacity to ensure availability of data
controls.prose: Adequate capacity to ensure availability of data shall be maintained. The standard binds all REs and is not listed in the Table 25 or Table 26 exemptions. The mandatory guideline, which applies to all REs except Self-certification REs, requires mechanisms, including alerts, to monitor capacity utilisation in real time, proactive handling of capacity needs, and compliance with SEBI circulars on capacity planning.
controls.guidance: probe-iac reads autoscaling limits, storage quotas and alert rules; runtime-probe-prod-env samples current utilisation of databases, disks and queues against alert thresholds. A critical store without a capacity alert is a medium finding. For Self-certification REs evidence adequate capacity under the standard only; the guideline's real-time capacity alerting and capacity-planning measures do not bind them, so their absence is not a finding for that tier.
evidenceExpected: Capacity monitoring dashboards and alert rules for critical data stores
Capacity planning report aligned to SEBI capacity-planning circulars

controls.title: Prevent data leaks; endpoint admin rights, client-side storage, certificates, macros and data migration
controls.prose: Measures against data leaks shall be implemented with appropriate tools to prevent data leakage. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires effective data protection, backup and recovery measures; blocking administrative rights on end-user devices by default with time-bound need-based grants; mobile and web application controls on handling PII and business data; no storage of sensitive information in HTML hidden fields, cookies or other client-side storage; timely renewal of digital certificates; control of VBA macros and permissible email attachment types; and a documented data-migration policy preserving integrity, completeness and consistency.
controls.guidance: execute-scr flags sensitive data written to localStorage, cookies without Secure/HttpOnly, or hidden form fields; runtime-probe-network-perimeter reports certificates expiring within 30 days; runtime-probe-identity-access checks local-admin group membership exports from the endpoint manager; runtime-probe-datapipeline confirms egress DLP or allow-listing on data exports.
evidenceExpected: DLP tooling configuration and incident reports
Endpoint policy showing local admin rights blocked by default
Certificate inventory with expiry dates
Email gateway attachment and macro policy
Approved data-migration policy

controls.title: Separate development and test environments from production; rigorous non-production testing
controls.prose: Development and testing environments shall be separated from production, and development of critical software shall have at least one non-production environment for rigorous testing before production deployment. The mandatory guideline for MIIs and Qualified REs requires separate production and non-production environments for all development and feature enhancements, system integration testing after development, addressing OWASP and SANS Top 25 class vulnerabilities during development, and recommends DevSecOps. Exempt for Mid-size REs (Table 26) and for Small-size and Self-certification REs (Table 25). FAQ Q52 allows Tier-3 hosting for development and test only if those environments hold no production or customer data.
controls.guidance: probe-iac and probe-dev-env verify that production and non-production run in separate accounts, subscriptions or clusters with no shared credentials or network paths; runtime-probe-devtest-env and runtime-probe-qa-env check for production data or customer PII in lower environments; probe-cicd-env confirms promotion gates require SIT results. Production data in a non-production environment is a high finding.
evidenceExpected: Account, subscription or cluster topology showing environment separation
Network policy or firewall rules blocking non-production to production paths
SIT reports gating production releases
Test data management evidence showing masked or synthetic data in non-production

controls.title: Integrity verification of software, firmware and information; source code or escrow for critical applications
controls.prose: MIIs shall put in place integrity mechanisms to verify software, firmware and information integrity of their critical systems and systems connected to them. The mandatory guideline for MIIs and Qualified REs requires obtaining source code of critical applications from third-party providers or, where not possible, a source-code escrow arrangement that includes all updates and patches (FAQ Q41 limits this to critical applications developed for the RE's sole use); time-bound mitigation of later-discovered vulnerabilities with closure timelines stipulated in vendor SLAs; third-party and software-vendor risk assessment proportionate to criticality; and formal agreements for maintenance and support. Exempt for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs (Tables 25-26).
controls.guidance: probe-cicd-env verifies image signing and provenance attestation (cosign, Sigstore, in-toto) in the release pipeline; probe-app-chart and runtime-probe-appcontainers verify admission policies enforce signature verification and that deployed digests match signed digests; refresh-vendor-ctx records escrow agreements and vulnerability-closure SLA clauses per vendor.
evidenceExpected: Signing and verification configuration for images, packages and firmware of critical systems
File integrity monitoring coverage for critical hosts
Source code receipts or escrow agreements covering updates and patches
Vendor SLAs with vulnerability-closure timelines

groups.title: Protect: Information Protection Processes and Procedures

controls.title: Baseline configuration with least functionality; hardening, port whitelisting and application whitelisting
controls.prose: A baseline configuration of IT systems shall be created and maintained incorporating security principles such as least functionality. The guidelines require IT, OT and IS infrastructure to be secure by design, by implementation and in operation; disabling unnecessary functions, ports, protocols and services; application directory whitelisting on all assets (mandatory for all REs except Small-size and Self-certification); and, as a mandatory guideline for all REs, deploying only hardened and vetted hardware and software with default usernames and passwords replaced, OS hardening, non-default service ports where applicable, blocking and monitoring unused open ports, firewall port whitelisting by business use with default deny, restricting PowerShell and wscript with script-block logging and transcription forwarded to a central log repository, and host-based firewalls to block RPC and SMB between endpoints.
controls.guidance: probe-iac evaluates security groups, NACLs and firewall policies for default-deny and whitelisted ports; probe-app-chart checks container securityContext, dropped capabilities and read-only root filesystems against the baseline in sdlc/policy.json; runtime-probe-prod-env and runtime-probe-appcontainers compare running configuration with CIS benchmark baselines; runtime-probe-network-perimeter lists unexpected open ports. Each drift from the approved baseline on a critical system is a finding.
evidenceExpected: Approved hardening baselines (CIS benchmarks or equivalent) per platform
Configuration compliance scan results against the baseline
Firewall rule review showing whitelisted ports and default deny
Application whitelisting policy and enforcement report

controls.title: Implement a system development life cycle
controls.prose: A System Development Life Cycle to manage systems shall be implemented. The SSDLC guidelines (PR.IP.S4 and S6) apply the lifecycle: business requirement documents stating security, session management, audit trail, logging, data integrity, event tracking and exception handling requirements; threat modelling and application security testing during development; reference to OWASP guidance such as ASVS; defence in depth; and assessment of new technologies before introducing them to critical systems.
controls.guidance: probe-sdlc compares sdlc/policy.json with actual repository practice (branch protection, required reviews, security requirements templates, threat-model artefacts); probe-cicd-env confirms security gates exist in pipelines. Missing lifecycle stages for a critical application are a medium finding.
evidenceExpected: Documented SDLC or SSDLC policy
Business requirement documents with security requirements for critical applications
Threat models for critical applications
Pipeline definitions showing security stages

controls.title: Configuration change control and change management with exception framework
controls.prose: REs shall put in place processes for configuration change control and change management. The guideline (all REs except Small-size and Self-certification) requires change management to be part of all third-party service agreements, to cover submission, planning with impact analysis and rollout plan, approval, implementation, post-implementation review and closure, and a defined framework for exceptions covering justification, duration, granting process, approving authority and periodic review. Exempt for Small-size and Self-certification REs on Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: probe-cicd-env and probe-sdlc verify production deployments trace to an approved change ticket and that emergency changes receive retrospective approval; probe-iac detects drift where infrastructure was changed outside the pipeline; impl-change-management records Maxwell's own proposed changes through the same lifecycle. Unapproved production change is a high finding.
evidenceExpected: Change management policy with exception framework
Sample of production changes with impact analysis, approval and post-implementation review
Drift detection report for infrastructure as code
Change clauses in third-party agreements

controls.title: Scan critical software for malicious code
controls.prose: REs shall thoroughly scan critical software and applications to ensure that no malicious code is present. The shared SSDLC guideline for PR.IP.S4 and S6 (all REs except Small-size and Self-certification) requires regression testing covering business logic, security controls, performance under stress-load and recovery conditions before new or modified systems go live, a vulnerability assessment for every production release, and VAPT for every major release.
controls.guidance: probe-cicd-env verifies malware, secret and dependency-confusion scanning of build artefacts and images (for example Trivy, Grype, ClamAV, OSV) with blocking gates; execute-scr runs static review for backdoors and obfuscated code; runtime-probe-appcontainers checks running images were scanned. A critical-system release with no scan record is a high finding.
evidenceExpected: Malware and composition scan results for each critical release
Regression test and vulnerability assessment reports per production release
VAPT report for each major release

controls.title: Undertaking from third-party providers that non-owned software is free of known vulnerabilities and malicious code
controls.prose: Where the source code of software is not owned by the RE, the RE shall obtain an undertaking or certificate from the third-party service provider stating that the software is free of known vulnerabilities, malware, malicious or fraudulent code and covert channels.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx records the undertaking reference, issue date and product version per vendor in vendors/<vendor_id>.json; refresh-soc raises a finding when a deployed third-party product version in the SBOM inventory lacks a current undertaking.
evidenceExpected: Signed vendor undertakings per product and version
Vendor register linking undertakings to deployed versions

controls.title: Software testing and certification addresses intended function, secure coding and known flaws
controls.prose: Testing and certification of software shall broadly verify that the product, version and modules function only as intended, that they are developed to secure design and coding practices and standards, and that known flaws and threats from insecure coding are addressed. The SSDLC guidelines shared with PR.IP.S4 apply.
controls.guidance: execute-scr performs secure code review against OWASP ASVS and CWE Top 25 for in-house critical applications; probe-cicd-env confirms SAST and DAST run and block on high findings. Evidence from external certification is attached by refresh-vendor-ctx for procured products.
evidenceExpected: SAST and DAST results with remediation status
Secure coding standard and code review records
Third-party certification reports for procured software

controls.title: Documented backup and recovery plan ensuring no data loss
controls.prose: REs shall document a backup and recovery plan of data to ensure that there is no data loss (see also RC.RP.S4).
controls.guidance: Attach the plan and verify that it names backup scope, frequency, retention, offsite and immutable copies for each critical data store in sdlc/metastore.json; probe-iac compares the plan with configured backup policies.
evidenceExpected: Approved backup and recovery plan covering every critical data store
Mapping of plan to configured backup policies

controls.title: Implement, test and maintain backups with periodic restoration drills
controls.prose: REs shall implement, test and maintain data backups and conduct drills for restoration of backup data on a periodic basis.
controls.guidance: probe-iac verifies backup schedules, cross-region or offsite copies and object lock; runtime-probe-prod-env reads the last successful backup and restore-test timestamps from the backup service. A critical store with no successful restore test in the period is a high finding citing sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S8 in regulatoryRefs (topic backup-rto-rpo; the sla-table has no sebi-cscrf-2024 row for it, so slaDueAt and slaBasis take the sla-table default for the finding's severity).
evidenceExpected: Backup job success reports for critical systems
Restore drill records with measured recovery time and data completeness

controls.title: Physical operating environment policies defined and adhered to
controls.prose: Policies and regulations regarding the physical operating environment for the RE's assets shall be defined and adhered to.
controls.guidance: Maxwell cannot probe physical facilities; record the data centre and colocation certifications (ANSI/TIA-942 rating, ISO 27001 scope) and CSP attestation reports via refresh-vendor-ctx, and treat missing attestations as observations for the cyber auditor.
evidenceExpected: Physical and environmental security policy
Data centre and colocation certifications and audit reports
CSP SOC 2 or ISO attestations covering physical controls

controls.title: Measure effectiveness of protective technologies against SLAs
controls.prose: The effectiveness of protective technologies shall be measured on a regular basis in line with the SLAs.
controls.guidance: report-audit-improvements computes coverage and time-to-remediate KPIs from the ledger and compares them with SLAs in sdlc/policy.json and vendor SLAs; refresh-soc raises an observation when a protective tool (EDR, WAF, DLP, SIEM) has no effectiveness metric for the period.
evidenceExpected: Protective technology effectiveness metrics (coverage, detection rate, false positives) against SLAs
Vendor SLA performance reports

controls.title: Response and recovery plans in place, regularly tested and updated
controls.prose: Response plans (incident response and business continuity) and recovery plans (incident recovery and disaster recovery) shall be put in place and regularly tested and updated.
controls.guidance: Attach the IR, BCP, incident recovery and DR plans with last test dates; refresh-soc reconciles test dates with RC.RP.S2 and RC.RP.S3 cadences and raises a finding when a plan was not tested in the period or not updated after an incident recorded in the ledger.
evidenceExpected: Incident response, BCP, incident recovery and DR plans with version history
Test reports for each plan in the financial year

controls.title: Develop and implement a vulnerability management plan
controls.prose: A vulnerability management plan shall be developed and implemented.
controls.guidance: cves/ enrichment, execute-scr, probe-cicd-env and runtime-probe-appcontainers feed vulnerability findings into the ledger; refresh-soc verifies each carries a dueAt from the SLA table and reports ageing against the plan. Absence of an approved plan or of scanning coverage for a critical system is a high finding.
evidenceExpected: Approved vulnerability management plan with severity-based timelines
Scan coverage report across critical systems
Vulnerability ageing report against plan timelines

controls.title: Comply with the SEBI Framework for Adoption of Cloud Services (MeitY-empanelled CSPs, data in India)
controls.prose: For applicable cloud instances, REs shall comply with SEBI's Framework for Adoption of Cloud Services by SEBI REs (circular SEBI/HO/ITD/ITD_VAPT/P/CIR/2023/033, 6 March 2023, CSCRF Annexure-J). Per the FAQs of 11 June 2025, storage and processing of data including logs must be done in data centres of MeitY-empanelled CSPs holding valid STQC certification or equivalent audit status, and REs must obtain assurance that all data centres in the chosen region meet this (Q48); the CSP must use only MeitY-empanelled infrastructure, with back-to-back compliance by subcontractors such as CDNs (Q47, Q50); a lapse in MeitY empanelment requires a risk assessment and action plan such as migration, renegotiation or exit (Q45); encryption keys and key-management operations must be handled within India, preferably with BYOK (Q26); contracts must delineate RE and CSP responsibilities, provide audit rights and visibility to the RE and SEBI, and require forensic cooperation (Q43, Q46); and the RE remains solely accountable for cloud services adopted (Q39, Q49). Hosted services and SaaS must meet the CSCRF hosted-service technical specification: ANSI/TIA-942 rated-4 or equivalent data centre, infrastructure equivalent to MeitY CSP empanelment audited by an STQC-empanelled or equivalent auditor, VAPT summaries available on demand, a readable copy of RE data in India if the data centre is abroad, no kill switch, and contractual delineation of responsibilities. CIR/2025/60 clause 5 mandates a dedicated HSM for MIIs and Qualified REs under the cloud framework.
controls.guidance: probe-iac records every cloud account, region and KMS or HSM configuration and flags regions outside India holding RE data, key rings managed outside India, and non-HSM keys for MIIs and Qualified REs; refresh-vendor-ctx records the CSP's current MeitY empanelment and STQC audit status, subcontractor list and contract clauses; runtime-probe-datapipeline records cross-border egress. Needs maintainer verification: the cloud framework clauses were taken from the FAQ restatement and CSCRF definitions, not fetched verbatim from the March 2023 circular in this run; confirm clause numbers and wording before citing them in a finding.
evidenceExpected: Current MeitY empanelment and STQC audit status of each CSP and region used
Region and key-management inventory showing data and keys within India
Cloud contracts with responsibility matrix, audit rights and forensic cooperation clauses
Hosted-service provider compliance with the CSCRF technical specification
Dedicated HSM evidence for MIIs and Qualified REs

params.label: SEBI cloud adoption framework circular to comply with
Minimum data centre rating for hosted services

controls.title: Only CERT-In empanelled IS auditors for external and cyber audits; auditor rotation and MD/CEO declaration
controls.prose: Only CERT-In empanelled IS auditing organisations shall be onboarded for external audits, including cyber audit, of the implementation of CSCRF standards and mandatory guidelines. The mandatory guideline (all REs except Self-certification) adds that an empanelled auditor may audit an RE for at most three consecutive years followed by a two-year cooling-off period; cyber audit reports carry an MD/CEO declaration per Annexure-B; revalidation VAPT and cyber audit are done in a time-bound manner; audit management covers calendar, planning, preparation, delivery, evaluation, reporting and follow-up; CERT-In auditee guidelines may be followed and Annexure-D auditor norms may be mandated; due diligence of audit process and tools is required; and MIIs and Qualified REs shall strive for an automated compliance tool and dashboard, preferably integrated with the log aggregator, available at cyber audit and SEBI inspection. CIR/2025/119 Part-D requires REs to follow the CERT-In Comprehensive Cyber Security Audit Policy Guidelines. Self-certification REs are exempt from periodic cyber audit (Section 8.1).
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx records the auditor's CERT-In empanelment validity and the consecutive years engaged; refresh-soc raises a finding when the empanelment has lapsed at audit start or when a fourth consecutive year is planned. Maxwell's ledger, KPI series and summary.md are candidate inputs for the automated compliance dashboard the guideline asks MIIs and Qualified REs to build.
evidenceExpected: CERT-In empanelment certificate of the audit firm valid for the audit period
Auditor engagement history showing rotation and cooling-off
MD/CEO declaration submitted with the cyber audit report
Audit calendar and follow-up tracker
Automated compliance dashboard (MIIs and Qualified REs)

params.label: Maximum consecutive years one empanelled auditor may audit the RE
Cooling-off period before the same auditor may audit again

controls.title: Application security and functional audit of all software used for critical systems
controls.prose: All software services, whether SaaS or hosted services, COTS, customised COTS or in-house developed, shall be certified for application security and functional audit, and COTS empanelled by stock exchanges or depositories shall be certified by STQC at empanelment. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires software for critical systems to pass DAST (against OWASP Top 10, SANS Top 25 and similar) and SAST, a functional audit covering data, report and transaction integrity, VAPT after every major release, integration of all critical-system logs with the SOC, audit of firewall, WAF, token and channel-identification configuration, an SBOM and a requirement traceability matrix; application security testing must include API security and API discovery. Exchanges and depositories test COTS through STQC before empanelment under an SOP; customised COTS and in-house software must be certified by a CERT-In empanelled auditor (FAQ Q53); SaaS and hosted services must evidence the CSCRF hosted-service technical specification and CSCRF function-level compliance.
controls.guidance: probe-cicd-env verifies SAST, DAST, API discovery and SBOM stages for each critical application and that results are retained; execute-scr supplies secure code review evidence; probe-agent-graph and runtime-probe-harnesses cover API and tool surfaces of AI-assisted services; runtime-probe-network-perimeter verifies WAF configuration; refresh-vendor-ctx records STQC or CERT-In auditor certificates for COTS and SaaS.
evidenceExpected: SAST, DAST and API security test reports per critical application release
Functional audit report covering data, report and transaction integrity
Certificate from a CERT-In empanelled auditor (in-house and customised COTS) or STQC (empanelled COTS)
SBOM and requirement traceability matrix per critical application
Firewall, WAF and token configuration audit

controls.title: MIIs obtain ISO 27001 certification covering PDC, DR, NDR, SOC and colocation
controls.prose: MIIs shall obtain ISO 27001 certification, with scope including at least the PDC site, DR site, NDR site, SOC and colocation facility; outsourced in-scope services must also be ISO 27001 certified (FAQ Q58). CSCRF also named Qualified REs, but CIR/2025/119 clause 6.11 made ISO 27001 recommended rather than mandatory for them. Exempt for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs (Tables 25-26). Timelines and evidence submission are in Section 4.2.
controls.guidance: Evidence-only: record certificate evidence against this standard, but raise findings only under Sec-4.2, which tracks certificate validity, scope and outsourced-site certificates, so one lapsed certificate never yields two findings. For Qualified REs record the certification status as an info observation.
evidenceExpected: ISO/IEC 27001 certificate and statement of applicability with required site scope
Certificates of third parties operating in-scope sites

controls.title: MIIs and Qualified REs follow CIS Critical Security Controls or equivalent
controls.prose: MIIs and Qualified REs shall follow globally recognised standards such as the latest version of CIS Critical Security Controls or equivalent prioritised safeguards to enhance cyber resilience (mandatory guideline). Exempt for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs (Tables 25-26).
controls.guidance: Maxwell maps its probe observations to CIS Controls v8.1 safeguards through the mappings in this catalog; report-audit-findings renders implementation-group coverage so the RE can evidence adoption.
evidenceExpected: CIS Controls (or equivalent) implementation assessment with safeguard coverage
Remediation plan for unimplemented safeguards

controls.title: Maintenance and repair of assets performed and logged with approved tools
controls.prose: Maintenance and repair of the RE's assets shall be performed and logged using approved and controlled tools. Exempt for Small-size and Self-certification REs on Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-prod-env checks that maintenance access uses the approved bastion or session manager with session logging enabled; probe-iac verifies maintenance tooling is provisioned through code. Unlogged maintenance sessions on critical systems are findings.
evidenceExpected: Maintenance log for critical systems
List of approved maintenance tools and session logging configuration

controls.title: Remote maintenance approved, logged and protected; trusted devices and monitored remote access
controls.prose: Remote maintenance of the RE's assets shall be approved, logged and performed in a manner that prevents unauthorised access. The mandatory guideline (all REs except Small-size and Self-certification) requires a remote access policy framework for secure access to data centre resources from home, remote access only from trusted client machines with controls such as host integrity checks and MAC-to-IP binding, risk mitigation whenever third-party service providers get remote access to data centre resources, and continuous monitoring of remote access with alerts on abnormal or unauthorised access. Exempt for Small-size and Self-certification REs on Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access verifies VPN or ZTNA device-posture enforcement, MFA and just-in-time access for third-party maintainers; runtime-probe-network-perimeter lists exposed remote-management ports (SSH, RDP, WinRM) reachable from the internet; refresh-soc checks SIEM alert rules for anomalous remote sessions.
evidenceExpected: Remote access policy framework
Device posture and trusted-device enforcement configuration
Third-party remote access approvals with time bounds
Remote access monitoring alert rules and sample alerts

controls.title: Severity-based patch management: High 1 week, Moderate 2 weeks, Low 1 month; no end-of-life critical systems
controls.prose: Patches shall be identified and categorised by severity, critical patches implemented at the earliest, and patches tested in a non-production environment before applying to DC and DR. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires patch identification, categorisation, prioritisation and implementation timeframes per category; regular patching of all operating systems and applications with virtual patching as an interim measure for zero-days; patches sourced only from authorised OEM sites; rigorous pre-production testing in an environment identical to production; replacement of critical-system hardware and software before end-of-life or end-of-support; compensatory controls such as virtual patching for legacy systems for at most 6 months with documented legitimate constraints; and procurement aligned to a technology refresh policy. For MIIs and Qualified REs, a patch management policy approved and reviewed at least annually by the IT Committee, post-patch capacity checks, quarterly patch-compliance reporting to the IT Committee, and patching at both PDC and DR within the upper limits of 1 week for High, 2 weeks for Moderate and 1 month for Low criticality patches, with emergency patches deployed within OEM-stipulated timelines. FAQ Q17 clarifies that VAPT findings caused by missing High patches are measured against the 1-week patch timeline rather than the 3-month VAPT closure window, and FAQ Q18 requires CSP and RE patch responsibilities to be demarcated in the contract. CIR/2025/119 lists patch timelines under exclusivity and the patch policy under equivalence for multi-regulated REs.
controls.guidance: cves/ enrichment and runtime-probe-appcontainers, runtime-probe-prod-env and probe-cicd-env detect missing patches and end-of-life components; refresh-soc flags virtual-patching compensations older than 6 months and end-of-life software on critical systems. The 1-week (High), 2-week (Moderate) and 1-month (Low) upper limits at both PDC and DR come from guideline item 11 and bind MIIs and Qualified REs only: for those tiers each finding carries slaBasis from the sla-table PR.MA.S3 patch-sla row for its severity (7, 14 or 30 days from patch publication). Guideline items 1-7 bind all REs but set no timeline, so for Mid-size, Small-size and Self-certification REs slaDueAt follows the sla-table defaults for the finding's severity. This control deliberately has no control-level slaDays. Findings cite PR.MA.S3, not the PR.PS.S6 id used in the soc record schema example.
evidenceExpected: Patch management policy approved and annually reviewed by the IT Committee
Patch compliance report per system and site (PDC and DR) with patch release and deployment dates
Quarterly patch compliance report to the IT Committee
Non-production patch test records
End-of-life register and virtual patching exceptions with expiry within 6 months

params.label: Upper limit to deploy High criticality patches at PDC and DR (MIIs and Qualified REs, guideline item 11)
Upper limit to deploy Moderate criticality patches at PDC and DR (MIIs and Qualified REs, guideline item 11)
Upper limit to deploy Low criticality patches at PDC and DR (MIIs and Qualified REs, guideline item 11)
Maximum period for virtual patching of legacy systems

controls.title: SOC operating 24x7x365 covering network, endpoints, personnel, malicious code and third-party activity
controls.prose: A Security Operations Centre shall be up and running 24x7x365 to monitor, prevent, predict, detect, investigate and respond to cyber threats, covering at least network, endpoints, physical environment, personnel activities, malicious code, unauthorised mobile code, third-party service provider activities and unauthorised personnel, devices, connections and software. All REs, except client-based stock brokers with fewer than 100 clients, shall employ SOC services using their own or group SOC, the Market SOC run by NSE and BSE (optionally NSDL or CDSL), or a third-party managed SOC; Small-size and Self-certification REs are mandated to onboard to Market SOC (Box Item 11; DE.CM guideline 1(c)-(d)), though those with their own or group SOC may keep it if they submit SOC efficacy reports (FAQ Q59-Q60; CIR/2025/119 clause 6.9). CIR/2025/60 exempts DPs and RTAs with fewer than 100 clients from SOC services and M-SOC, and exempts self-certification portfolio managers and AIF/VCF managers with fewer than 100 clients only from mandatory M-SOC, so those must still employ own, group or third-party SOC services (see Sec-2.Exemptions). MIIs shall run a dedicated 24x7x365 C-SOC per SEBI circular CIR/MRD/CSC/148/2018 (Annexure-M). All critical-system logs must be integrated with the SOC (PR.IP.S15 guideline 1(d)). Responsibility for CSCRF compliance stays with the RE even when on M-SOC.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx records the SOC model (own, group, M-SOC, third-party) and contract; runtime-probe-prod-env and probe-iac confirm log forwarders and EDR agents are deployed on every critical asset in sdlc/metastore.json; runtime-probe-datapipeline verifies ingestion is live by checking last-event timestamps per source. A critical asset not reporting to the SOC is a high finding.
evidenceExpected: SOC model declaration and contract (own, group, Market SOC onboarding confirmation or MSSP agreement)
SOC coverage report reconciling log sources and EDR agents with the critical asset inventory
24x7x365 roster or MSSP SLA
C-SOC framework compliance for MIIs

params.label: Client count below which the SOC-service or M-SOC exemption applies (see Sec-2.Exemptions for scope by entity type)

controls.title: Continuous security monitoring mechanisms in the SOC for timely detection
controls.prose: Appropriate continuous security monitoring mechanisms shall be established in the SOC for timely detection of anomalous or malicious activities. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires monitoring of security events and alerts to detect unauthorised or malicious activity, unauthorised changes and access, and unauthorised copying or transmission of data held in a contractual or fiduciary capacity by internal and external parties, including monitoring security logs of internet-exposed systems, applications and network devices for anomalies, and generating alerts on unauthorised or abnormal system activity, transmission errors or unusual online transactions.
controls.guidance: probe-iac verifies cloud audit trails, flow logs and threat-detection services are enabled in every account and region; refresh-soc checks detection rules exist for Maxwell probe findings classes such as public buckets, privileged role grants and unusual egress; runtime-probe-network-perimeter confirms internet-facing systems ship logs. Missing audit trail in any production account is a high finding.
evidenceExpected: SIEM use-case and detection rule catalogue mapped to critical assets
Cloud audit trail and flow log configuration per account and region
Sample alerts for unusual transactions and unauthorised changes

controls.title: Investigate all anomalies and alerts within stipulated time; measure SOC functional efficacy
controls.prose: All anomalies and alerts generated shall be properly monitored and investigated within the stipulated time. The guidelines require MIIs and Qualified REs to measure SOC functional efficacy half-yearly using the Annexure-N quantified method (five domains: coverage of assets by SOC technologies 25 percent, SOC operations 25 percent, competency of SOC personnel 20 percent, SOC governance 15 percent, SOC enrichments and enhancements 15 percent), and REs using a third-party managed SOC or Market SOC to obtain an Annexure-N efficacy report from their provider yearly. The original guideline requiring BAS, CART and decoy deployment was made recommendatory by CIR/2025/119 clause 6.5 (consider threat simulation, vulnerability management and decoys in consultation with the IT Committee). Global REs may submit global SOC efficacy if controls apply uniformly (FAQ Q64) and may add tools such as IDAM, FIM and SSO (FAQ Q65). CIR/2025/119 Part-A allows equivalence with a primary regulator for SOC efficacy.
controls.guidance: refresh-soc tracks alert investigation time from the SOC case system and the last Annexure-N score as parameters, raising a finding when efficacy was not measured in the half-year (MIIs and Qualified REs) or year (M-SOC and MSSP users); report-audit-findings prints the five domain scores. The asset-coverage domain can be computed from refresh-metastore inventory against SOC integration evidence.
evidenceExpected: Alert triage records with investigation timestamps against defined SLAs
Annexure-N SOC functional efficacy report with domain scores
Provider-issued yearly SOC efficacy report for M-SOC or MSSP users

params.label: SOC functional efficacy reviews per year for MIIs and Qualified REs

controls.title: Monitor capacity utilisation of critical systems and networks
controls.prose: Capacity utilisation shall be monitored for all critical systems. The mandatory guideline (all REs except Small-size and Self-certification) requires monitoring, tuning and projection of IT resource use; mechanisms to monitor capacity of critical systems and networks for resilience and timely detection of attacks; capacity management across data storage, processing power and communications bandwidth; and both proactive (capacity in change management) and reactive (threshold alerts) capacity management. FAQ Q66 clarifies the focus is anomalous utilisation, alerts and unusual network traffic. Exempt for Small-size and Self-certification REs on Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: probe-iac reads autoscaling policies and utilisation alarms for compute, storage and network; runtime-probe-prod-env samples utilisation and alert state; runtime-probe-network-perimeter checks DDoS and anomalous-traffic alerting on edge services.
evidenceExpected: Capacity dashboards and threshold alerts for storage, compute and bandwidth of critical systems
Capacity projection report and change-management capacity checks
Anomalous traffic alert rules

controls.title: Cybersecurity, configuration, implementation and change management audits and VAPT to detect vulnerabilities
controls.prose: Cybersecurity audit, configuration audit, implementation audit, change management audit and VAPT shall be conducted to detect vulnerabilities in the IT environment. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires regular cyber audit and VAPT with the CSCRF scope (Annexure-L), in-depth evaluation through simulation of actual attacks, audit scope covering all critical systems and infrastructure components (network and security devices, load balancers, servers, databases, applications, remote access points, WAN, LAN and public IP systems, websites) and other operational IT systems, VAPT before commissioning new systems that are or connect to critical systems, and time-bound revalidation after closure. Stock brokers and DPs that are Qualified or Mid-size REs shall report vulnerabilities discovered in COTS or empanelled applications to the vendor and the exchange or depository in a timely manner. Periodicity, submission and closure timelines are in Section 4.3 (VAPT) and 4.4 (cyber audit).
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter, runtime-probe-prod-env and execute-scr provide continuous pre-audit evidence; refresh-soc imports auditor VAPT and cyber audit observations as findings with slaBasis topics vapt-cadence or audit-cadence and verifies a VAPT record exists before any newly commissioned critical system appears in sdlc/metastore.json.
evidenceExpected: VAPT reports covering the Annexure-L scope with revalidation reports
Cyber audit, configuration audit and change management audit reports
Pre-commissioning VAPT reports for new critical systems
Vulnerability notifications to COTS vendors and exchanges or depositories (stock brokers and DPs)

controls.title: Roles and responsibilities for detection defined for accountability
controls.prose: Roles and responsibilities for detection shall be defined to ensure accountability.
controls.guidance: Evidence a RACI for detection (SOC tiers, use-case owners, escalation to CISO) and the contact roles in details.json; refresh-soc raises a finding when no owner is recorded for a detection use case covering a critical system.
evidenceExpected: Detection RACI and SOC escalation matrix
Use-case ownership register

controls.title: Test detection processes with playbooks and use cases
controls.prose: REs shall ensure that detection processes are tested by developing playbooks and use cases.
controls.guidance: refresh-soc checks each detection use case has a recorded test (atomic test, purple-team exercise or replay) in the period; runtime-probe-sandboxes can host safe detection tests where the rules of engagement permit.
evidenceExpected: Detection playbooks and use-case library
Detection test results per use case with date

controls.title: Communicate event detection information per regulatory requirements and policy
controls.prose: Event detection information shall be communicated as per the regulatory requirements and organisational policies.
controls.guidance: Link detection escalation to RS.CO.S2 reporting: refresh-soc checks that every incident record in the ledger with a regulatory threshold has regulatorReportRefs within the CSCRF and CERT-In windows.
evidenceExpected: Detection-to-escalation communication procedure
Incident tickets showing escalation timestamps

controls.title: Half-yearly goal-based red teaming and CART; lessons shared with SEBI within 3 months
controls.prose: MIIs and Qualified REs shall conduct goal-based adversarial simulation red teaming exercises periodically to identify weaknesses in cyber defence. The mandatory guideline requires red teaming half-yearly using red and blue teams, deployment of a CART solution for continuous automated security testing and attack-surface visibility, a red team independent of the function tested (employees and/or external experts), results placed before the IT Committee and governing Board, lessons learned shared with SEBI within 3 months of completion, and IT Committee monitoring of remediation. FAQ Q56 confirms KRAs as Qualified REs need BAS and CART. CIR/2025/119 Part-A allows equivalence with a primary regulator's red-teaming requirement. Exempt for Mid-size and lower categories (Tables 25-26).
controls.guidance: Import red team observations into the ledger as findings citing sebi-cscrf-2024:DE.DP.S4 in regulatoryRefs (topic red-team-cadence; the sla-table has no sebi-cscrf-2024 row for it, so slaDueAt and slaBasis take the sla-table default for the finding's severity); refresh-soc tracks the last two exercise dates, the SEBI submission date and remediation. runtime-probe-network-perimeter output supplements CART attack-surface evidence. Maxwell never performs red teaming itself.
evidenceExpected: Red team exercise reports for each half of the financial year
IT Committee and Board minutes reviewing results
Lessons-learned submission to SEBI within 3 months
CART solution configuration and reports

params.label: Red teaming exercises per financial year
Months after completion to share lessons learned with SEBI

controls.title: Quarterly threat hunting and regular compromise assessment
controls.prose: REs shall conduct threat hunting and compromise assessment on a regular basis. The mandatory guideline for MIIs and Qualified REs requires proactively searching for hidden and undetected threats and threat hunting leveraging threat intelligence, IOCs and IOAs on a quarterly basis. REs are encouraged to supplement NCIIPC and CERT-In intelligence with industry, commercial and peer feeds (FAQ Q67). Exempt for Mid-size and lower categories (Tables 25-26).
controls.guidance: refresh-soc tracks quarterly hunt reports and raises a finding when a quarter passes without one; runtime-probe-prod-env can supply read-only IOC sweeps (hash, domain and process lookups) as supporting evidence within the rules of engagement.
evidenceExpected: Quarterly threat hunting reports with hypotheses, data sources and outcomes
Compromise assessment report
Threat intelligence feeds used

params.label: Threat hunting exercises per quarter

controls.title: Board-approved Cyber Crisis Management Plan with scenario-based SOPs and incident response plan
controls.prose: A comprehensive Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP) shall be documented with scenario-based SOPs, include the incident response management plan, and be triggered as soon as an incident occurs. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires an up-to-date CCMP in line with CERT-In's national CCMP, approved by the Board, partners or proprietor; an incident response management plan defining responsibilities of employees and outsourced staff; SOPs for response and recovery for various attacks; for MIIs, an SOP for incidents reported by REs under their supervision; and adherence to the Annexure-O SOP for reporting incidents to SEBI.
controls.guidance: Attach the CCMP with Board approval date; refresh-soc raises a finding when it is not approved, not aligned to the national CCMP, or not revised after an incident in the ledger. runtime-probe-harnesses and probe-agent-graph confirm AI agent and tool incidents are covered by a scenario where such systems are in scope.
evidenceExpected: CCMP aligned to CERT-In national CCMP with Board approval
Scenario-based incident response SOPs
MII SOP for incidents reported by supervised REs

controls.title: Optimise timely response: awareness, training, skills, playbooks and knowledge base
controls.prose: REs shall optimise their ability to respond in a timely and appropriate manner to adverse conditions, stresses, attacks or their indicators so as to maintain operations and limit consequences. The guideline (all REs except Small-size and Self-certification) requires cybersecurity awareness, training for relevant teams, developing or hiring appropriately skilled people, cyber playbooks and a knowledge database of known adverse conditions and attacks. Exempt for Small-size and Self-certification REs on Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: Evidence playbook library and responder training; refresh-soc checks that playbooks exist for the incident classes in Annexure-O Table 35 and for ransomware, data exfiltration and DDoS.
evidenceExpected: Incident response playbooks and knowledge base
Responder training and skills matrix

controls.title: Board-approved contingency plans, COOP, exercises and incident response and recovery plans
controls.prose: REs shall prepare contingency plans, a continuity of operations plan (COOP), training, exercises and incident response and recovery plans for their systems and infrastructure and have them approved by the Board, partners or proprietor. Exempt for Small-size and Self-certification REs on Market SOC (Table 25).
controls.guidance: Attach approvals and the plan set; refresh-soc cross-checks review cadence with RS.IM.S1 (half-yearly for MIIs and Qualified REs, once in two years for Mid-size).
evidenceExpected: Contingency plan and COOP with Board approval
Exercise schedule and reports

controls.title: Contain and mitigate incidents; mitigate or accept newly identified vulnerabilities
controls.prose: Cybersecurity incidents shall be contained and mitigated, and newly identified vulnerabilities shall be mitigated or documented as accepted risks.
controls.guidance: Every incident record in the ledger must link to containment actions and every newly identified vulnerability finding must reach resolved or accepted-risk status with a risk record; refresh-soc raises a finding for findings open with neither mitigation nor documented acceptance.
evidenceExpected: Incident containment and mitigation records
Risk acceptance register for unmitigated vulnerabilities with approvals

controls.title: Onboard to CERT-In Cyber Swachhta Kendra and close CSK alerts time-bound
controls.prose: MIIs and Qualified REs shall onboard to CERT-In's Cyber Swachhta Kendra (CSK) and other CERT-In initiatives. The mandatory guideline requires collaborating with CSK to trace bots and vulnerable services on their public IP addresses, receiving its alerts, closing them in a time-bound manner and placing observations that need longer to close before the IT Committee. Exempt for Mid-size and lower categories (Tables 25-26).
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter enumerates public IPs and exposed services so CSK alerts can be reconciled; refresh-soc imports CSK alerts as findings and flags those open beyond the RE's defined window without IT Committee reference.
evidenceExpected: CSK onboarding confirmation with registered public IP ranges
CSK alert log with closure dates
IT Committee minutes for long-running CSK observations

groups.title: Respond: Incident Response Reporting and Communication

controls.title: SOP documenting personnel roles and responsibilities for incident response
controls.prose: An SOP documenting the roles and responsibilities of the RE's personnel for cybersecurity incident response shall be prepared and implemented.
controls.guidance: Attach the SOP and confirm the designated officer and CISO contact roles in details.json match it; refresh-soc raises a finding when the SOP names people no longer in role.
evidenceExpected: Incident response roles SOP
Current incident contact list

controls.title: Report cyber incidents to SEBI and CERT-In within 6 hours; SEBI portal within 24 hours; quarterly reports
controls.prose: Cybersecurity incidents falling under the CERT-In Directions shall be notified to SEBI, CERT-In and NCIIPC (as applicable) within the stipulated time, and all other incidents as per guidelines. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires any cyber attack, incident or breach under the CERT-In Directions to be notified to SEBI and CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing or detection or being brought to notice, to SEBI via mkt_incidents@sebi.gov.in within 6 hours with details on the SEBI Incident Reporting Portal within 24 hours; stock brokers and DPs also report to the stock exchanges or depositories within 6 hours; all other incidents are reported to SEBI, CERT-In and NCIIPC (as applicable) within 24 hours; entities designated Protected Systems report to NCIIPC; threat intelligence is shared on the SEBI portal; quarterly reports on attacks, threats, incidents, breaches and mitigation are submitted within 15 days after the quarters ending June, September, December and March; useful details are shared in masked form using TLP; and regular progress reports such as RCA and forensic reports are provided while SEBI processes the incident. For MIIs and Qualified REs the IT Committee discusses response plans and coordination, stakeholder contact details are kept current, and customers are notified through alternate channels of transactions above a customer-set value (all REs). CIR/2025/119 clause 6.4 replaced the press-release and customer-notification-by-impact guideline with action per the approved CCMP. Non-reporting of a known incident attracts regulatory action (Annexure-O B.1).
controls.guidance: Every incident record in the soc ledger with a CERT-In Annexure-I category carries regulatorReportRefs with slaBasis topic incident-reporting and dueAt of detection plus 6 hours for SEBI, CERT-In and (for brokers and DPs) the exchange or depository, and plus 24 hours for the SEBI portal; refresh-soc raises a critical finding when any window was missed. report-audit-findings lists the quarterly report submissions against the 15-day deadline.
evidenceExpected: Incident notifications to SEBI (email and portal), CERT-In, NCIIPC and exchanges or depositories with timestamps
Detection timestamps from SOC case records
Quarterly incident reports with submission acknowledgements
Threat intelligence submissions on the SEBI portal

params.label: Hours from noticing a CERT-In reportable incident to notify SEBI, CERT-In and the exchange or depository
Hours to report incident details on the SEBI Incident Reporting Portal
Hours to report all other cybersecurity incidents
Days after quarter end to submit the quarterly incident report to SEBI

controls.title: Coordinate with stakeholders per the CCMP during an incident
controls.prose: In the event of a cybersecurity incident, REs shall coordinate with stakeholders as per their CCMP.
controls.guidance: Evidence stakeholder communications logged in the incident record; refresh-soc checks each high or critical incident lists stakeholder coordination actions.
evidenceExpected: Stakeholder communication log per incident
CCMP stakeholder contact matrix

controls.title: Receive, analyse and respond to vulnerabilities and incidents disclosed from internal and external sources
controls.prose: Processes shall be established to receive, analyse and respond to vulnerabilities and incidents disclosed to the RE from internal and external sources such as internal testing, security bulletins or security researchers. The shared mandatory guideline for RS.AN.S1-S3 requires investigation of alerts to prevent spread and resolve incidents, collection and preservation of incident data (system logs, network traffic, forensic images), analysis of scope, cause and impact, and forensically sound preservation of evidence.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter checks for a published security.txt or disclosure contact; cves/ enrichment and refresh-soc show advisories and researcher reports enter the ledger with triage timestamps.
evidenceExpected: Vulnerability disclosure policy and intake channel
Triage records for disclosed vulnerabilities and bulletins

controls.title: Categorise incidents per the CCMP and Annexure-O severity classification
controls.prose: Cybersecurity incidents shall be categorised in line with the categorisation in the RE's CCMP. Annexure-O Table 35 classifies incidents as Low (probes or scans on external systems, credential-compromise intelligence, isolated known malware), Medium (targeted recon, attempted attacks with no impact, widespread known malware, isolated new malware, clicked phishing, data corruption reports), High (attacks with limited operational impact, widespread new malware, unauthorised server or network access, unexpected configuration changes, SEBI impersonation, data exfiltration, outbound phishing) or Critical (successful penetration or DoS with significant impact, ransomware, exfiltration of market-sensitive data, widespread data corruption impacting operations); any incident that disrupts normal service delivery must be High or Critical, and classification is reviewed by the IT Committee before reports go to SEBI.
controls.guidance: The incident record severity in the soc ledger follows Table 35 exactly (Low, Medium, High, Critical map to Maxwell low, medium, high, critical); refresh-soc raises a finding when an incident with service disruption is recorded below high.
evidenceExpected: CCMP incident classification aligned to Annexure-O Table 35
IT Committee review of classification per reported incident

controls.title: Detailed investigation and forensic analysis to find root cause, modus operandi and lateral movement
controls.prose: Detailed investigation of incidents and alerts, with forensic analysis as appropriate, shall identify the root cause, the threat actor's modus operandi and any lateral movement, and prevent recurrence. For all High and Critical incidents the RE shall submit a forensic audit or investigation report; for Low and Medium incidents only if the RCA is inconclusive or SEBI or HPSC-CS directs; forensic audits must be performed by third-party auditors selected after due diligence or Indian government forensic labs (Annexure-O clause 4; FAQ Q75-Q76). The forensic report is due within at most 75 days of reporting the incident, with a timeline for fixing its observations and an IT Committee-reviewed closure report.
controls.guidance: Incident records link forensic evidence references (hash-stamped disk images, memory captures, log exports) as evidenceRef; refresh-soc raises a finding when a high or critical incident has no forensic report by reporting date plus 75 days.
evidenceExpected: Investigation report per incident identifying root cause, TTPs and lateral movement
Forensic audit report by an independent third party for High and Critical incidents
Chain of custody for preserved evidence
Forensic closure report reviewed by the IT Committee

params.label: Maximum days from reporting the incident to submit the forensic audit report

controls.title: Root cause analysis identifying failed controls and posture improvements
controls.prose: RCA shall be done to determine the people, process and technology gaps that led to the incident and to strengthen posture against similar incidents. The shared mandatory guideline for RS.AN.S4-S5 requires RCA identifying the failed control and underlying cause, forensic analysis as appropriate, thorough analysis of any loss or destruction of data or systems with lessons fed into recovery planning, a detailed incident report with recommendations, and a compromise assessment through a CERT-In empanelled IS auditing organisation. Annexure-O Table 36 requires, from the date of reporting, an interim report within 3 days, mitigation measures within 7 days, the RCA report within 30 days (extendable by SEBI case by case), and incident VAPT with closure reports within 45 days; reports are reviewed by the IT Committee before submission, and deficient reports may be resubmitted within 15 days of being notified.
controls.guidance: Incident records carry dueAt parameters for interim (3 days), mitigation (7 days), RCA (30 days) and incident VAPT (45 days); refresh-soc raises a finding for each missed milestone and links RCA gaps to new findings and initiatives through impl-change-management.
evidenceExpected: Interim report within 3 days and mitigation measures within 7 days
RCA report within 30 days with cause, chronology, impacted systems and corrective actions
Incident VAPT and closure report within 45 days
Compromise assessment by a CERT-In empanelled auditor
IT Committee review report submitted with the RCA

params.label: Days from reporting to submit the interim report
