Days from reporting to submit incident VAPT and closure reports
Additional days to resubmit a report SEBI finds deficient

controls.title: Mandatory impact analysis; RCA and forensics per Annexure-O; HPSC-CS review
controls.prose: Impact analysis of every incident shall be mandatorily conducted, with RCA and forensic analysis as appropriate performed per the Annexure-O SOP 'Classification and Handling of Cybersecurity Incidents'. The SOP requires capturing whether the incident response plan was followed, containment, stakeholder communication, mitigation, RCA, lessons learned, closure of RCA gaps and independent audit findings. High and Critical incidents at MIIs, Qualified REs and Mid-size REs are reviewed by SEBI's HPSC-CS, whose recommendations must be implemented within the timelines it sets; other incidents are processed by SEBI, which agrees a remediation plan and timelines with the RE. Non-adherence to the SOP attracts regulatory action.
controls.guidance: Incident records include an impact analysis (affected systems, data, customers, financial and market impact) before closure; refresh-soc tracks HPSC-CS or SEBI recommendations as initiatives with due dates and raises a finding when overdue.
evidenceExpected: Impact analysis per incident
Annexure-O lifecycle checklist per incident
HPSC-CS or SEBI recommendations and implementation evidence

controls.title: Incorporate lessons learned into response plans, training and testing
controls.prose: Lessons learned from incident handling shall be incorporated into incident response plans, training and testing, and resulting changes implemented. The guideline requires REs (except Self-certification) to periodically review and update contingency plans, COOP, training exercises and incident response and recovery plans including the CCMP, where periodically means half-yearly for MIIs and Qualified REs and once in two years for Mid-size and Small-size REs (footnote 32), and all REs to update response and recovery plans including the CCMP after any incident.
controls.guidance: refresh-soc checks the plan version history against incident closure dates in the ledger and against the half-yearly or biennial review cadence for the RE category.
evidenceExpected: Plan revision history showing post-incident and periodic updates
Lessons-learned register linked to plan changes

params.label: Plan reviews per year for MIIs and Qualified REs
Years between plan reviews for Mid-size and Small-size REs

controls.title: Communicate response plan changes to designated key personnel with Board approval
controls.prose: Changes to the response plan shall be communicated to the RE's designated key personnel, and updates to contingency plans, COOP, training exercises and incident response and recovery plans shall be communicated and approved by the Board, partners or proprietor.
controls.guidance: Evidence distribution records and Board approval of each plan version; refresh-soc raises a finding when the approved version differs from the version in circulation.
evidenceExpected: Distribution acknowledgements for revised plans
Board approval of plan updates

controls.title: Scenario-based recovery plans; golden images, spare capacity and immutable backups
controls.prose: The RE's recovery plan shall have different cyber-scenario-based classifications. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires scenario-based response and recovery plans in the CCMP tailored to the business model, timely restoration plans such as alternate services, tests that challenge response, resumption and recovery assumptions including governance and communication and involve critical service providers, vendors and linked REs, and use of the Annexure-C recovery plan template. For MIIs and Qualified REs it further requires regularly updated golden images of critical systems at an offsite location, exploring spare hardware in an isolated environment kept ready and tested (cloud high-availability is an acceptable alternative, FAQ Q72, Q74), precautions to keep images and backups undamaged, isolated and immutable or air-gapped backups against ransomware, and regular business continuity drills including recovery from ransomware affecting both PDC and DR.
controls.guidance: probe-iac verifies immutable or object-locked backup vaults in a separate account, golden image pipelines with recent builds, and cross-region recovery infrastructure; runtime-probe-prod-env reads last golden-image build dates. Absence of an immutable backup copy for a critical system of an MII or Qualified RE is a high finding.
evidenceExpected: Scenario-based recovery plan per Annexure-C
Golden image inventory with build dates and offsite storage (MIIs and Qualified REs)
Immutable or air-gapped backup configuration
Ransomware recovery drill report covering PDC and DR

controls.title: RTO of 2 hours and RPO of 15 minutes; half-yearly scenario-based cyber resilience testing
controls.prose: RTO and RPO as specified by SEBI shall be mandated while executing the recovery plan. As published, the mandatory guideline for all REs required an incident to be declared a disaster within 30 minutes of disruption of critical systems, an RTO of 2 hours per IOSCO and an RPO of 15 minutes; CIR/2025/119 clause 6.10 now reads it as: design and test systems and processes to safely resume critical operations within two hours of disruption even in extreme but plausible scenarios, exercise judgement so resumption does not escalate risk, plan with the IT Committee for scenarios where the objective is not met, and RPO of 15 minutes for critical systems per SEBI's 22 March 2021 BCP-DR circular. For MIIs and Qualified REs it requires comprehensive scenario-based cyber resilience testing at least twice per financial year (six-monthly) including extreme plausible scenarios devised with the IT Committee, periodic backup restore testing, inclusion of critical third parties and linked REs, results placed before the IT Committee, lessons learned shared with SEBI within 3 months of the testing period, and IT Committee tracking of observations. Live drills are required; table-top exercises do not satisfy the requirement (FAQ Q70), and all scenarios must be covered within one audit period (FAQ Q69).
controls.guidance: probe-iac reads replication lag objectives, backup frequency and multi-region failover configuration and compares them with 15-minute RPO and 2-hour RTO; runtime-probe-prod-env reads current replication lag and last failover test results; refresh-soc records drill dates, measured RTO and RPO as parameters and raises a finding citing sebi-cscrf-2024:RC.RP.S2 in regulatoryRefs (topic backup-rto-rpo; the sla-table has no sebi-cscrf-2024 row for it, so slaDueAt and slaBasis take the sla-table default for the finding's severity) when a measured value exceeds the objective or a half-year passes without testing.
evidenceExpected: Business impact analysis with RTO 2 hours and RPO 15 minutes for critical systems
Replication and backup configuration evidencing RPO
Live cyber resilience test reports for each half-year with measured RTO and RPO
IT Committee review and lessons-learned submission to SEBI within 3 months

params.label: Recovery time objective for resumption of critical operations
Recovery point objective for critical systems
Minutes after disruption to declare a disaster (original CSCRF text, superseded in wording by CIR/2025/119 clause 6.10)
Scenario-based cyber resilience tests per financial year (MIIs and Qualified REs)
Months after the testing period to share lessons learned with SEBI

controls.title: Periodic drills testing different recovery scenarios
controls.prose: REs shall periodically conduct drills to test different recovery scenarios and the adequacy and effectiveness of the response and recovery plan (mandatory guideline for all REs). CSCRF Table 15 sets recovery drills half-yearly for MIIs and Qualified REs and annually for others.
controls.guidance: refresh-soc tracks drill dates and outcomes; report-audit-findings shows drills against the category cadence. runtime-probe-prod-env can confirm failover state after a drill without initiating one.
evidenceExpected: Drill calendar and reports with scenarios, participants and outcomes
Post-drill improvement actions

controls.title: IT Committee-approved backup and recovery plan with offsite data and image backups; quarterly offline backup tests
controls.prose: A backup and recovery plan of data shall be documented to ensure no data loss. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires the plan to be approved by the IT Committee, combine policies and software solutions with restoration guidance, cover backup of data and server images, keep backups at off-site locations, and include SEBI-prescribed RTO and RPO. MIIs and Qualified REs shall also maintain offline encrypted backups and test them at least quarterly for confidentiality, integrity and availability.
controls.guidance: probe-iac verifies backup policies include server images and data, off-site or cross-account copies and encryption; runtime-probe-prod-env reads last restore-test dates; refresh-soc raises a finding when an MII or Qualified RE has no quarterly offline backup test.
evidenceExpected: Backup and recovery plan approved by the IT Committee
Backup configuration for data and server images with off-site copies
Quarterly offline encrypted backup test reports (MIIs and Qualified REs)

params.label: Offline encrypted backup tests per quarter (MIIs and Qualified REs)

controls.title: Public relations management per the recovery plan during an incident
controls.prose: Public relations management as defined in the recovery plan shall be undertaken in the event of a cybersecurity incident; the guideline requires recovery plans, including stakeholder coordination and internal and external communication, to be discussed with the IT Committee. CIR/2025/119 clause 6.4 directs REs to act per their approved CCMP rather than a fixed press-release rule.
controls.guidance: Evidence the PR section of the recovery plan and communications issued for past incidents in the ledger.
evidenceExpected: Recovery plan communication section discussed with the IT Committee
Public statements issued for incidents

controls.title: Communicate recovery activities to internal and external stakeholders and management
controls.prose: REs shall communicate recovery activities to internal and external stakeholders as well as executive and management teams.
controls.guidance: Incident records in the ledger reference recovery status updates to management and stakeholders.
evidenceExpected: Recovery status communications to management and stakeholders

controls.title: Inform stakeholders of actions taken during recovery
controls.prose: REs shall inform all related stakeholders of the actions taken during the recovery process.
controls.guidance: As RC.CO.S2; refresh-soc checks closure records include a stakeholder notice of recovery actions.
evidenceExpected: Post-recovery stakeholder notices

controls.title: Update recovery plans with lessons learned; BCP-DR supports cyber resilience
controls.prose: Recovery plans shall be updated and improved to incorporate lessons learned from cybersecurity incidents. The guideline requires the RE's BCP-DR capabilities to support cyber resilience objectives and rapid recovery of critical operations, and REs to try to incorporate lessons from incidents reported by other REs.
controls.guidance: refresh-soc links post-incident lessons to recovery plan revisions; refresh-ctx surfaces peer-RE incident advisories as context.
evidenceExpected: Recovery plan revisions referencing incident lessons
Record of peer incident lessons considered

controls.title: Upgrade cyber resilience through periodic drills; meet RTO for interconnected systems
controls.prose: The RE's cyber resilience capabilities shall be upgraded through periodic drills to ensure safe and timely restoration of critical operations. The mandatory guideline for all REs requires meeting RTO for all interconnected systems and networks through capacity upgrades and periodic coordinated resilience testing, and improving the recovery plan after analysing drill learnings.
controls.guidance: refresh-soc compares measured RTO across interconnected systems in drill reports with the 2-hour objective and tracks improvement actions as initiatives.
evidenceExpected: Coordinated resilience test reports for interconnected systems
Improvement actions from drills with closure status

controls.title: Strategies to anticipate new attack vectors and reduce attack surface
controls.prose: REs shall formulate strategies to anticipate new attack vectors by removing or applying new controls to compensate for identified vulnerabilities or weaknesses, reducing or manipulating attack surfaces, and proactively orienting controls, practices and capabilities to prospective, emerging or potential threats. The shared guideline for EV.ST.S1-S3 covers threat modelling based on risk assessment, attack-surface reduction, proactive examination of controls, adaptive changes to requirements, architecture, design, configuration, acquisition and operations, rapid deployment and integration of services on premises and in cloud, data correlation using mathematical models and machine learning, and audit logging on different operating systems. The standard binds all REs ('REs shall') and is not listed in the Table 25 or Table 26 exemptions; only the shared EV.ST.S1-S3 guideline carries the applicability 'All REs except small, self-certification REs' (page 131), so Small-size and Self-certification REs remain bound by the standard but not by the guideline measures.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter trends the external attack surface over time; probe-agent-graph and runtime-probe-harnesses surface emerging AI and agentic attack surfaces; report-audit-improvements reports attack-surface reduction as an improvement metric. For Small-size and Self-certification REs assess only the standard text and do not raise findings for the guideline-only measures, since the guideline (not the standard) excludes them.
evidenceExpected: Threat models updated for emerging attack vectors
Attack-surface inventory trend and reduction actions

controls.title: Demonstrate heterogeneity to minimise common-mode failures
controls.prose: REs shall demonstrate heterogeneity to minimise common-mode failures, particularly threat events exploiting common vulnerabilities. The shared guideline applies different audit and logging regimes at different architectural layers, assesses feasibility of diverse operating systems, and maintains extra capacity for storage, processing and communications. The standard binds all REs ('REs shall') and is not listed in the Table 25 or Table 26 exemptions; only the shared EV.ST.S1-S3 guideline carries the applicability 'All REs except small, self-certification REs' (page 131), so Small-size and Self-certification REs remain bound by the standard but not by the guideline measures.
controls.guidance: refresh-metastore and runtime-probe-prod-env summarise OS, runtime and CSP diversity of critical systems and their DR counterparts; refresh-soc records single-technology concentration as a risk rather than a finding. For Small-size and Self-certification REs assess only the standard text and do not raise findings for the guideline-only measures, since the guideline (not the standard) excludes them.
evidenceExpected: Technology diversity assessment for critical systems and DR
Layered logging design

controls.title: Confirm post-incident modification of business functions and processes
controls.prose: REs shall confirm post-incident modification of business functions and supporting processes to handle adversity and environmental change, incorporating incident learning to evolve their cyber resilience posture. The standard binds all REs ('REs shall') and is not listed in the Table 25 or Table 26 exemptions; only the shared EV.ST.S1-S3 guideline carries the applicability 'All REs except small, self-certification REs' (page 131), so Small-size and Self-certification REs remain bound by the standard but not by the guideline measures.
controls.guidance: impl-change-management tracks post-incident initiatives to completion; refresh-soc verifies each closed high or critical incident links to at least one completed initiative. For Small-size and Self-certification REs assess only the standard text and do not raise findings for the guideline-only measures, since the guideline (not the standard) excludes them.
evidenceExpected: Post-incident change initiatives with completion evidence

controls.title: MIIs and Qualified REs continuously adapt and evolve against new threats
controls.prose: MIIs and Qualified REs shall continuously adapt and evolve to counter new cybersecurity threats and challenges. The standard binds only MIIs and Qualified REs by its own wording; Small-size and Self-certification REs are also listed as exempt in Table 25.
controls.guidance: report-audit-improvements shows the trend of findings, time to remediation and suggestion acceptance as evidence of continuous evolution; impl-auto-improvement proposes improvements from recurring finding classes.
evidenceExpected: Cyber resilience improvement roadmap with progress
KPI trend showing improvement over consecutive periods

controls.title: Mid-size and Small-size REs periodically evaluate cyber resilience posture
controls.prose: Mid-size and Small-size REs shall periodically evaluate their cyber resilience posture; CSCRF Table 15 sets this at least annually. Self-certification REs are exempt (Section 8.1).
controls.guidance: report-audit-findings produces the posture evaluation from the ledger; refresh-soc raises a finding when no evaluation exists for the financial year.
evidenceExpected: Annual cyber resilience posture evaluation report
